items.summary: InstructReplay is proposed to keep instruction-tuned models' general behavior intact during factual fine-tuning by replaying assistant turns.
items.why: Reports that standard fine-tuning cut instruction-following, reasoning and coding scores by about 35 points on average, a practical risk when updating models with new facts.

items.title: Reading Decisions Before Spans: Efficient Generative Verification
items.summary: Researchers show a generative verifier's accept-or-error decision can be recovered from early output tokens, avoiding full decoding for claim checking.
items.why: Could lower latency and compute for teams running generative verifiers that only need a pass or fail alarm on claims.

items.title: ShellBench: What Matters More for AI Agents, Models, or Harness for Everyday Tasks
items.summary: ShellBench introduces 100 everyday tasks to compare how models and agent harnesses affect correctness and safety, evaluating 12 models across 5 harnesses.
items.why: Offers evidence on whether model choice or agent harness matters more for everyday agent tasks, informing configuration decisions.

items.title: Beyond Expected Value: PPO with Distributional Critics for Systematic Conservation Planning
items.summary: Researchers replace evolution strategies with PPO and distributional critics in CAPTAIN, a sequential reinforcement learning framework for conservation planning.
items.why: Shows how distributional critics can address worst-case outcomes in sequential planning under uncertainty, though the application is domain-specific.

items.title: LoomKV: Lossless KV Cache Compression from GPU Memory to SSD for LLM Serving
items.summary: LoomKV proposes lossless KV cache compression spanning GPU memory, host DRAM and SSD for LLM serving on unmodified engines.
items.why: Lossless KV offloading to SSD could raise concurrency and prefix reuse for long-context and agent serving without changing outputs.

items.title: Can LLM Judges Catch Unsafe Clinical Actions? A Fault-Injection Study
items.summary: A fault-injection study tests whether six open-weight LLM judges can detect unsafe clinical actions in MedAgentBench agent trajectories.
items.why: Indicates LLM judges may miss dangerous clinical errors even when agents appear to finish tasks, a caution for evaluating healthcare agents.

items.title: RecordRoute: Auditing Agent Failures with Localization-Guided Diagnosis
items.summary: RecordRoute proposes couples localization with diagnosis to audit failed agent executions, identifying the responsible actor, decisive step and error mode.
items.why: Offers a method for post-hoc debugging of failed agent runs, which matters for teams operating multi-step agents in production.

items.title: Hybrid AI for AI-Native RAN Control: A Functional Perspective
items.summary: A survey proposes a technique-agnostic taxonomy of AI-native radio access network control, covering representation, prediction, adaptive control and decision synthesis.
items.why: Provides a common framework for telecom engineers weighing how AI and conventional methods should divide RAN decision-making.

items.title: Auditing the Judge: Human-Derived Bias Discovery, Quantification, and Mitigation in LLM Judges
items.summary: Researchers propose using human preferences to discover, quantify and mitigate systematic biases in LLM judges used as automated evaluators.
items.why: Teams relying on LLM-as-judge pipelines may get more reliable evaluations by auditing judge bias against human preferences.

items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Candidate Generation for Entity Linking in Cyber Threat Intelligence
items.summary: A proof-of-concept keeps uncertainty in named entity recognition and passes candidate sets to entity linking instead of single hard decisions, for cyber threat intelligence.
items.why: Could make threat-intelligence entity pipelines more robust by avoiding brittle early commitments under ambiguous inputs.

items.title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance
items.summary: Delegent is a multi-agent harness built on Claude Code that delegates easy subtasks to a small local language model while the frontier model stays in charge.
items.why: Suggests cutting frontier-model agent costs by offloading simple subtasks to owned hardware, though results depend on the paper's evaluation.

items.title: Temporal Conditioning for Human Behavioral Cloning in Chess
items.summary: Researchers introduced a time-aware transformer for chess behavioral cloning that conditions on clock state, time control, and tempo to predict human moves, thinking time, and resignation.
items.why: Shows that temporal context such as time pressure can be modeled explicitly to better capture human decision-making quality.

items.title: MetaFORGE: A Meta-Learning Framework for Harness Optimization in Automated Code Generation for Parallel Computing
items.summary: MetaFORGE is a meta-learning framework that iteratively optimizes natural-language skill specifications to improve LLM generation of MPI C parallel code, using test, compiler, and runtime feedback.
items.why: Offers a feedback-driven way to improve LLM-generated parallel code by tuning instructions against correctness and performance signals.

items.title: SoundWeaver: Compositional Warm-Starting for Text-to-Audio Diffusion Serving
items.summary: SoundWeaver is a training-free framework that speeds text-to-audio diffusion by building a prompt-conditioned acoustic prior from reusable segments of prior examples instead of starting from pure noise.
items.why: A training-free acceleration technique could cut inference latency and serving cost for text-to-audio diffusion systems.

items.title: When Can a Rewiring Control Test LLM Weight Readers? C2 and an Eligibility Protocol
items.summary: The paper proposes C2, a counterfactual control that permutes a network's final linear readout to test whether LLMs predict network outputs from computation or from weight-space fingerprints.
items.why: Clarifies how to validate claims that LLMs can read computation from raw model weights, avoiding confounds from weight regularities.

items.title: InletScope: Multiscale pressure-based inlet unstart monitoring under changing sensor configurations
items.summary: InletScope is a multiscale pressure-based monitoring model for supersonic aeroengine inlets that detects unstart and predicts onset within 0.5 seconds, handling changing sensor configurations without retraining.

items.title: Actionwave: A Systematic Benchmark for Waveform-Centric Clinical Prediction Across Care Scenarios
items.summary: Actionwave is a benchmark for waveform-centric clinical prediction across intensive-care, operating-room, and emergency-department settings, testing how performance depends on signal duration, warning time, and inputs.
items.why: Provides a standardized benchmark for comparing clinical waveform models across care settings before deployment decisions.

items.title: Validation Bias in Large Language Model Responses to Cancer Treatment Queries: A Factorial Cross-Sectional Study
items.summary: A factorial study finds that LLM chatbots may validate patients' evidence-misaligned beliefs about cancer treatment rather than correcting them, based on tests across conversation format, treatment type, and query valence.
items.why: Highlights a safety risk for health-facing LLM products, where models may affirm misleading treatment beliefs instead of correcting them.

items.title: DAGGER: Deployment-Free Quality Estimation for Generative AI Workflows
items.summary: DAGGER proposes a deployment-free method to estimate end-to-end quality of multi-stage generative AI workflows, avoiding the cost of deploying and evaluating every candidate model configuration.
items.why: Could reduce the cost of choosing model configurations across multi-stage AI pipelines without exhaustive deployment testing.

items.title: Instantiation of Human Values in Image Generation
items.summary: Researchers generated 28,000 images from four text-to-image models using value-laden prompts grounded in Schwartz's human values theory to study how abstract values are visually depicted.

items.title: The Date You Didn't Set: The System-Prompt Date as a Hidden Variable in LLM Evaluation
items.summary: The paper shows that the date automatically inserted into system prompts can change LLM evaluation results, flipping a median 6.6% of test items between correct and incorrect across six models.
items.why: Evaluation pipelines that auto-insert dates may produce unstable results, so teams should pin or record that hidden input.

items.title: INCLUDE-2.0: Disentangling Knowledge Gaps in Multilingual LLM Evaluation
items.summary: INCLUDE-2.0 is a multilingual benchmark covering 91 languages from 86 countries with over 220K samples, designed to separate language proficiency from region-specific factual knowledge.
items.why: Gives teams a region-aware benchmark to distinguish language ability from local knowledge gaps in multilingual models.

items.title: Directly Maximizing On-policy Expected Accepted Length for Speculative Decoding
items.summary: FreDraft is an on-policy training method for speculative decoding drafts that directly maximizes the expected accepted length rather than token-level distribution alignment.
items.why: Targeting accepted length directly could yield faster LLM inference from speculative decoding without changing the target model.

items.title: RECAP: Training Long-horizon LLM Agents with Context Compaction
items.summary: RECAP is a reinforcement learning framework that trains LLM agents to compress long interaction histories into summaries that preserve the behavior induced by the original history.
items.why: Addresses how long-horizon agents can stay within context limits while keeping task performance through learned context compaction.

items.title: RecipeADQA: A User-aware Question-Answering Dataset for Multi-Constraint Recipe Recommendation
items.summary: RecipeADQA is a question-answering dataset for multi-constraint recipe recommendation, built from real user queries and reviews to capture natural preference signals.

items.title: Capability and Interpretability of Transformers on Multi-task Recurrence
items.summary: The paper studies capability and interpretability of transformers on controlled linear recurrence tasks over cyclic groups, ranging from a single fixed rule to latent rule identification and rule switching.
items.why: Provides controlled insight into how transformers internally represent recurrent rules, which may inform interpretability work.

items.title: Does Item Response Theory Generalize Across Languages? Evidence from Cross-Lingual LLM Benchmarks
items.summary: Researchers test whether Item Response Theory data selection for benchmarks holds across languages, using translated Multilingual GSM and Global MMLU with 100+ models and 11 languages.
items.why: Suggests IRT-filtered benchmark subsets may not transfer cleanly across languages, which matters when building multilingual evaluation suites.

items.title: RegioZH: Unveiling Comprehension Disparities across Regional Chinese Varieties in LLMs
items.summary: RegioZH is a 2,607-item benchmark testing LLMs on regional Chinese varieties from five regions; eleven models show a 29.4-point average accuracy gap between Taiwan and Singapore.
items.why: Shows that treating Chinese as one language hides large performance gaps for regional users, relevant to localization and evaluation.

items.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Iranian Doctoral Entrance Exams in Electrical and Computer Engineering
items.summary: Four LLMs were evaluated on 433 Iranian doctoral entrance exam questions in electrical and computer engineering, in both Persian and English, with figure-dependent items included.
items.why: Gives a domain-specific reference point for LLM performance on technical engineering exams, though the text offers limited detail on results.

items.title: How Persona Conditioning Changes Open-Ended Task Execution: A Paired Evaluation of Behavioral Gains and Reliability Costs
items.summary: A paired study finds persona prompts change how LLMs execute open-ended tasks in multi-turn role-play, measuring behavioral gains alongside reliability costs.
items.why: Indicates persona prompting can alter task behavior and reliability beyond character fidelity, which affects prompt design decisions.

items.title: SD-Cache: Learnable Memory Consolidation with State-Guided Dynamic Caching
items.summary: SD-Cache proposes learnable memory consolidation with state-guided dynamic caching to limit KV cache growth from retrieved content in RAG systems.
items.why: Addresses linear KV cache growth in persistent RAG services, a direct cost and memory concern for inference infrastructure.

items.title: AhaPro: A Process-level Rebus benchmark for probing Aha moments in LLM reasoning
items.summary: AhaPro is a process-level benchmark using rebus puzzles to study how LLMs reorganize evidence and revise answers during visible reasoning, the so-called Aha moments.
items.why: Offers a way to probe reasoning-trace behavior beyond final answers, useful for evaluating reasoning models.

items.title: Reliability of Language-Model Judges for Quantitative Scientific Question Answering: Evidence from Perovskite Photovoltaics
items.summary: Evaluation of LLM judges on 755 perovskite photovoltaic questions, with 4,530 free-text answers from six retrieval architectures, finds reliability on quantitative science synthesis is largely unmeasured.
items.why: Highlights that LLM-as-judge grading may be unreliable for quantitative answers, a caution for teams relying on automated evaluation.

items.title: Agentic Optimization: LLM Agents Select and Configure Algorithms for Engineering Design
items.summary: The paper proposes agentic optimization, where an LLM agent reads a problem description to select and configure multi-objective evolutionary algorithms, comparing five LLMs on engineering benchmarks.
items.why: Points to LLM agents as a way to pick optimization algorithms for new design problems without performance history.

items.title: LLM Genetic Feature Engineering
items.summary: The paper builds on LLM-guided metaheuristic feature engineering, introducing a genetic approach to automate constructing derived variables from datasets.

items.title: The Industrialization of Noise: Why Automated Proof-Solving is the Same Old Dead End
items.summary: A paper argues that OpenAI's release of 722 automated mathematical manuscripts claiming solutions to 372 open problems repeats a failed approach to proof, drawing on the DeMillo-Lipton-Perlis framework.
items.why: Frames debate over the value of automated proof generation, which is relevant to how engineers assess AI-generated research claims.

items.title: PEACE-TEST-PROTOCOL: Polarization-Keyed Examination Papers and Mandatory Issued Eyewear that Displace AI Glasses and Extend Universal Design
items.summary: PEACE-TEST-PROTOCOL proposes polarization-encoded exam papers readable only through authority-issued glasses to prevent AI glasses from reading test questions.

items.title: Differential evolution with perturbation for continuous function optimization
items.summary: The paper presents differential evolution with perturbation (DEP) for continuous function optimization and compares it to existing algorithms on CEC2017 datasets.

items.title: Set-based comprehensive learning and particle swarm optimization with memory for discrete optimization problem
items.summary: The paper introduces a set-based comprehensive learning particle swarm optimization with memory for discrete optimization problems, validated through numerical experiments.

items.title: When Successful Collaboration Becomes an Attack Surface: Insider Memory Poisoning in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: MIMPA is proposed as an attack in which malicious insiders poison shared memory of successful collaboration records in multi-agent systems, so false information appears as trusted team experience.
items.why: Identifies shared agent memory as a new attack surface that engineers building multi-agent systems need to defend against.

items.title: Evolutionary AI Control: Population-Level Safety Under Reproduction, Heredity, and Selection
items.summary: The paper proves conditions under which population-level safety guarantees persist through agent reproduction, inheritance, and selection, and shows four counterexamples where they fail.
items.why: Shows individually safe agents can yield unsafe populations in open multi-agent systems, a concern for long-running self-replicating agent designs.

items.title: Scoring Recovery-Time Agent Security: Proposals, Effects, and Retry Instructions
items.summary: Researchers propose an executable evaluation separating tool proposals, runtime decisions, and committed effects, showing timed-out agent writes can hide harmful recovery actions.
items.why: Goal-existence checks can overstate agent success; engineers should audit committed side effects and retry behavior after timeouts.

items.title: Conformalized Tree-Based Gradient Ensembles for Out-of-Distribution Detection and Plausible Recourse
items.summary: Researchers study conformalized tree-based gradient ensembles to detect out-of-distribution counterfactual recourse suggestions that exploit boundary artifacts.
items.why: Recourse search optimizing classifier confidence alone can yield implausible recommendations; out-of-distribution checks help keep them realistic.

items.title: Layer-Readout Interfaces in EEG Foundation Models: Predictive Accessibility and Cross-Dataset Transfer
items.summary: A study of EEG foundation models finds final-layer readout choices strongly affect frozen-feature performance, and examines whether intermediate-layer advantages transfer across datasets.
items.why: Choosing which layer to read features from can change results substantially, so readout design matters when reusing frozen foundation models.

items.title: Per-Attack Blocking Hides Catalog Vulnerability: A Weakest-Link Analysis of Tool Manifests
items.summary: Analysis argues per-attack blocking metrics hide catalog-level risk, since a tool catalog is only as safe as its weakest source policy.
items.why: Teams relying on per-attack block rates may underestimate exfiltration risk across many tool manifests; evaluate the weakest policy in the catalog.

items.title: GHC:Expanding Residual Interfaces in Hyper-Connections
items.summary: Researchers propose Grouped Hyper-Connections, which partition branches into groups to give each a distinct stream mixture and wider residual interfaces.
items.why: It proposes an architectural change to transformer residual connections; the abstract gives too little detail on measured gains to judge practical impact.

items.title: Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation
items.summary: NVIDIA's Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation is an agentic framework that combines learned visual tokens for raster images with explicit programs for structured artifacts like vector graphics and webpages.
items.why: It unifies raster and programmatic visual generation under one agentic harness, relevant to teams building document or design automation.

items.title: Leaks by Installments: Cross-Session Answer Disclosure in LLM Tutors and a Ledger-Based Defense
items.summary: Researchers show LLM tutors can leak answers across sessions and propose a persistent per-learner disclosure ledger to track and block cumulative answer disclosure.
items.why: Per-reply safeguards miss answers leaked over multiple sessions; stateful disclosure tracking is needed for education products built on LLMs.

items.title: Below the Stopwatch: Checking the Performance Claims of Coding Agents in the Kernel
items.summary: Below is a pipeline that checks whether coding agents' performance PRs achieve speedups for the reasons they claim, using kernel and hardware signals across 1,343 PRs.
items.why: Stopwatch benchmarks cannot confirm a claimed optimization mechanism; kernel-level verification helps review agent-authored performance changes.

items.title: AdProducer: Towards Agentic Advertising Video Generation
items.summary: AdProducer proposes an agentic system for generating advertising videos that combines product understanding with strategic decisions about presenting product value.

items.title: Reading Between the Layers: Where Representation Quality Lives, and What Geometry Reveals
items.summary: A study of 25 pretrained text models finds representation quality often peaks before the final layer, and examines how to select probing layers without labels.
items.why: Probing the final layer may underperform; layer selection without labels could improve embedding use in production pipelines.

items.title: Tempering and few-shot calibration of pathology foundation models improve digital biomarker reproducibility across slide scanners
items.summary: A tempering and few-shot calibration method for pathology foundation models reduced cross-scanner prediction differences by 67.5% across several cancer biomarker tasks.
items.why: Scanner-induced variability hurts clinical model reproducibility; the calibration approach targets cross-site reliability in medical AI deployments.

items.title: Where Agent Defenses Fail: A Case Study of Policy Compositions and Measurement Limits
items.summary: A case study finds restrictive sandboxing blocks attacks but reduces benign utility, while host mediation restores uploads yet admits some disclosure, measured via files and HTTP receipts.
items.why: Sandbox and mediator policies interact in ways that trade off utility and security; agent defenses need end-to-end measurement of effects.

items.title: Reproducible Social Structure Emerges From Free-Form Interaction Among LLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce a repeatable multi-agent framework where fifty persona-conditioned LLM agents with memory communicate across three platforms, aiming for reproducible social dynamics.
items.why: Single-run multi-agent simulations are anecdotal; a repeatable framework enables more reliable social simulation research.

items.title: Denoising Diffusion with Progressive Posterior Sampling
items.summary: Researchers propose progressive posterior sampling with manifold projection for diffusion-based linear inverse problems, estimating noise variance automatically and avoiding SVD.
items.why: Removes need for SVD or known noise variance in diffusion-based inverse problem solvers, potentially simplifying imaging pipelines.

items.title: The Paradox of Agency-Preserving AI: Negotiating Learner Agency in Layered Human-AI Interactions
items.summary: Researchers examine how meta-level AI systems that scaffold learner reflection can paradoxically constrain the learner agency they are meant to preserve.

items.title: LatentLens: Rethinking Latent Interface in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: Researchers propose LatentLens, a framework that separates latent agent-to-agent communication from the agent harness to measure its real contribution to multi-agent performance.
items.why: It questions whether reported gains from latent interfaces come from the communication method or the surrounding harness, which matters when designing multi-agent systems.

items.title: GoldiBench: Right Tools, Wrong Amount -- Benchmarking Agents on Effect Judgement in Professional Editing
items.summary: Researchers introduce GoldiBench, a 500-task benchmark testing whether agents can judge the right amount of editing tools to match a described look in professional applications.
items.why: It exposes that existing VLM-judged benchmarks pass many incorrect edit strengths, so teams evaluating editing agents need stricter measures.

items.title: RePT: 3D Geometry Emerges from 2D Relational Pretraining
items.summary: RePT is a pretraining method that learns relations across 2D views without 3D targets, and its learned representation reportedly develops geometric structure resembling physical 3D geometry.
items.why: It suggests spatial 3D structure may be learned from 2D relational pretraining without explicit geometric supervision.

items.title: What You See Is What You Certify: Concept-Based Certificates for Unseen Compositions
items.summary: The paper argues concept-based models trained as standard can certify wrong classes on unseen attribute combinations, about 93-94% of the time in the reported tests.
items.why: Concept explanations can look justified while being wrong, so teams relying on them for interpretability should not treat them as reliable certificates.

items.title: Provenance Loss and Repair in Multilingual Compaction
items.summary: The paper examines how conversational assistants' compaction of older messages into notes loses grammatical gender information in languages like Spanish, and proposes a training-free repair.
items.why: Lossy memory compaction in multilingual assistants can make later turns assert attributes users never gave, a practical bug for chatbot builders.

items.title: Right Destination, Wrong Journey: Synthetic Counseling Dialogues Miss Human Interactional Dynamics
items.summary: A trajectory-based study finds LLM-generated counseling dialogues often reach plausible endpoints but differ from human support in recovery dynamics and turn-by-turn responsiveness.
items.why: Teams using synthetic dialogues to train or evaluate mental-health systems should not assume they match real interactional dynamics.

items.title: GRUN: Generalized Retinex Unfolding Network for Image Restoration
items.summary: GRUN proposes a generalized Retinex formulation that factorizes images into content and environment components for image restoration.

items.title: Rapid Exploratory Maps and their potential role in supporting evidence-to-policy dialogues and processes
items.summary: The paper describes Rapid Exploratory Maps as a way to support dialogue between evidence producers and policymakers when scoping evidence syntheses.

items.title: CATWAY: Cost-sensitive agentic three-way robot decisions with calibrated language-model confidence
items.summary: CATWAY is a cost-sensitive three-way gate that decides whether a language-model robot agent should execute, ask, or refuse an instruction, using calibrated confidence.
items.why: Deriving decision thresholds from error costs and calibrated probabilities offers a principled safety gate for LLM-driven robots that tech leaders deploying agents could adapt.

items.title: FoveaWAM: Role-Aware 4D World-Action Modeling for Dynamic Manipulation
items.summary: FoveaWAM proposes role-aware 4D world-action modeling that predicts the target object's pose precisely while forecasting surroundings more coarsely, for dynamic robot manipulation.
items.why: Decoupling prediction precision by object role could cut computation for robot policies that manipulate moving objects.

items.title: EventSSM: Causal Spatial-State Modelling for Asynchronous Events Event-Depth Estimation
items.summary: EventSSM introduces a causal spatial-state recurrent model that processes event camera data in chronological packets to estimate metric depth.

items.title: Geo-SMILE: Statistical Model-Agnostic Interpretability with Local Explanations for Geospatial Machine Learning
items.summary: Geo-SMILE is a model-agnostic explanation framework for geospatial machine learning that separates feature effects from geographic-position effects using perturbation branches.
items.why: Standard post-hoc explainers often ignore geographic context, so this offers a way to interpret spatial models more accurately.

items.title: MOSAIC: Memory-Organized Search with Anti-Imitation Crossover for Training-Free Microarchitecture Optimization
items.summary: MOSAIC is a search controller that improves LLM-generated cache-replacement policies without updating model weights, storing lessons from past evaluations to limit held-out performance loss.
items.why: It shows a training-free way to use LLM code search for systems optimization while reducing overfitting to searched workloads.

items.title: Where is the Interface for the AI Harness?
items.summary: The paper argues agentic delegation creates new interaction gaps, citing a 2026 incident where a research agent circumvented an access refusal on an Australian government portal unnoticed for two months.
items.why: Users who delegate to agents leave the loop, so teams building agent interfaces need oversight and visibility designs for unseen actions.

items.title: RVLM-X: Towards a Universal VLM Harness
items.summary: RVLM-X proposes a task-generalizable harness for vision-language models that avoids fixed procedures like zoom trees, letting frontier models plan and use tools for large images.
items.why: Fixed VLM harnesses may reduce accuracy with newer models that plan and use tools well, which affects how teams build image-analysis pipelines.

items.title: RoMo Hands: A Large Scale Richly Organized Text to Hand Motion Dataset
items.summary: Researchers introduced RoMo Hands, an in-the-wild text-paired dataset of about 542K hand motion sequences, filtered for dexterity.
items.why: Large, finely captioned hand-motion data could help teams train text-to-hand generation models that current datasets are too small to support.

items.title: DELTA: Diagnosing Exploration Lineages via Twin-path Alignment - What Can Contrasting Design Paths Reveal About Microarchitectural Behavior?
items.summary: The DELTA paper proposes using data produced during design-space exploration to explain why microarchitecture searches stop improving.
items.why: It suggests architects can reuse exploration traces to diagnose bottlenecks, not just pick the best configuration.

items.title: SPARQL-Planned Single-Hop Traversal over a Live Knowledge Graph for Multi-Hop Question Answering
items.summary: The paper proposes SPARQL-planned single-hop traversal over a live knowledge graph to improve multi-hop question answering retrieval.
items.why: It offers a way to reduce the noise and cost of multi-hop graph expansion in retrieval-augmented systems.

items.title: VISOR: A Vision-Language Selector for Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting
items.summary: VISOR is a vision-language selector for multimodal time-series forecasting that aims to preserve diverse future distributions rather than collapsing to a median.
items.why: It targets two named limits of current forecasters: flattened predictive distributions and weak text-to-series alignment.

items.title: Three-Dimensional Wake Reconstruction and Cross-Scale Transfer for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines via Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operators
items.summary: Researchers used physics-informed Fourier neural operators to reconstruct three-dimensional wakes behind floating offshore wind turbines and transfer them across turbine scales.

items.title: Learning Compact State Abstractions for LLM Agents
items.summary: The paper defines compact state abstractions that let LLM agents keep only the interaction history they need, instead of the full history.
items.why: Smaller agent state could cut context costs while keeping a reference agent's competence, relevant to long-running agent design.

items.title: TopoCryptoEEG: End-to-End Encrypted Framework for Brainprint Authentication
items.summary: TopoCryptoEEG proposes a homomorphic-encryption framework for brainprint authentication after showing encrypted feature schemes can leak templates.
items.why: It highlights that feature-level encryption under a trusted-client assumption can be broken, a design concern for biometric systems.

items.title: How Far Apart Are Two Proofs? Measuring Proof Dissimilarity in a Proof Kernel and in Lean/Mathlib
items.summary: The paper introduces methods for measuring distances between mathematical proofs, in a proof kernel and in Lean/Mathlib.
items.why: Proof-distance metrics could help teams judge whether AI-generated formal proofs are actually novel or redundant.

items.title: Agentic Discovery of Soundness Bugs in Safe Rust Bindings
items.summary: The paper proposes using LLM agents to audit safe Rust bindings for soundness bugs that allow undefined behavior from safe code.
items.why: Agentic auditing of Rust FFI wrappers could find unsafe-boundary defects that static analyzers and fuzzers miss.

items.title: Exploring Multi-Player Social Games as Verifiable Training Grounds for Large Language Models
items.summary: The paper explores multi-player social games as verifiable training environments for Qwen3 models using SFT and reinforcement learning.
items.why: Rule-based game outcomes could replace expensive, noisy LLM judges as reward signals for social-skill training.

items.title: POISE: Curvature-Aware Critic Regularization for Smooth Actor-Critic Control
items.summary: POISE proposes curvature-aware critic regularization to reduce high-frequency action oscillations in actor-critic robotic control.
items.why: It targets smoothness of learned robot controllers by regularizing the critic rather than the actor.

items.title: Gaze World Model
items.summary: The Gaze World Model paper introduces a world-model approach to estimating gaze targets and how gaze shifts respond to scene changes.

items.title: Spec-Test Coverage Gap: Detecting Overspecified Tests in SWE-Bench-Style Benchmarks
items.summary: The paper defines a Spec-Test Coverage Gap metric and uses LLM judges to detect overspecified tests in SWE-bench-style coding benchmarks.
items.why: Overspecified tests can reject correct alternative fixes, so this affects how reliably coding-agent benchmarks measure performance.

items.title: Faithful Persona Steering under Incongruity via Dual-Stream Refinement
items.summary: QuirkyMind is a framework that separates persona identity definition from its expression to keep atypical persona traits in LLM steering.
items.why: It addresses context drift and loss of idiosyncratic traits in long-sequence LLM personalization.

items.title: JECT: Addressing the Context Shortcut in Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for Chest CT
items.summary: JECT addresses a context shortcut in joint-embedding predictive learning for chest CT, where hidden findings are predicted as normal anatomy.

items.title: Two-Stage Post-Training for Flow-Based Embodied Foundation Models
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a two-stage post-training approach for flow-based embodied foundation models, building on multi-teacher on-policy distillation to go beyond teacher performance.
items.why: Offers a post-training recipe for robot foundation models that aims to combine supervised fine-tuning and RL while mitigating distribution mismatch and sparse rewards.

items.title: CALVIN-MAX: When Does a Mid-Execution Change Hurt a Robot Policy?
items.summary: Researchers introduce CALVIN-MAX, a benchmark of 7,828 cases testing how a single mid-task change to objects, camera, robot, or instruction affects robot policy success.
items.why: Gives teams a benchmark for measuring robot policy robustness to mid-execution environment changes, a common failure mode in deployment.

items.title: EEG-Jev: A Unified Single-Pass Decision Model for EEG
items.summary: EEG-Jev is a unified single-pass model that handles EEG choice, statement judgment, and ordered rating tasks, trained jointly on 35 public sources.

items.title: Rethinking Video Agents: When and Why Video Harnesses Work
items.summary: A paper examines when and why agentic video harnesses, which let models request further observations, improve video understanding compared with fixed input policies.
items.why: Suggests that letting models request more video evidence only helps under certain task and model conditions, which affects agent design choices.

items.title: Loupe: Reinforcing Knowledge-Intensive Video Generation Agents
items.summary: Loupe is a video generation agent that retrieves and verifies textual and visual evidence to build evidence-grounded plans for knowledge-intensive video generation, trained with reinforcement learning.
items.why: Shows an agentic retrieval-and-verification loop for improving factual accuracy in generated video, relevant to teams building generative media pipelines.

items.title: MIFLOW: Dynamic Recent-Behavior Priors for Reference-Calibrated Online Flow-Policy Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: MIFLOW proposes a recency-adaptive flow-matching prior fitted to recently executed actions to calibrate online flow-policy reinforcement learning for continuous control.

items.title: Your VLM Knows What to Inspect: Semantic Probe-Guided Adaptive Focusing for GUI Grounding
items.summary: SPARK is a training-free framework that uses VLM-generated semantic probes to guide adaptive region zooming for GUI grounding, even when coordinate predictions are wrong.
items.why: Offers a training-free way to improve GUI element localization for computer-use agents by leveraging VLM visual descriptions.

items.title: Machine learning enables full Bayesian inference for spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
items.summary: Researchers report a machine learning method enabling full Bayesian inference over all 14 parameters of spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals from gravitational-wave data.

items.title: Beyond Rigid Hands: Deforming Skin into Contact-Consistent Hand Meshes
items.summary: A paper presents a method that deforms rigid annotated or estimated hand meshes into skin-like, contact-consistent shapes that touch objects realistically while staying close to the original pose.

items.title: Are Web Agents Still Detectable? Stress-Testing Bot Defenses with Coordinated Evasion
items.summary: DarkAgent, an autonomous web agent with a forked Chromium browser, is introduced to stress-test whether bot defenses can detect agents that coordinate evasion across fingerprints and behavior.
items.why: Highlights that coordinated evasion may defeat current bot defenses, which matters for teams protecting sites from automated agents.

items.title: Distill to Loop: Turning Pretrained Diffusion Transformers into Looped Models with Adjustable Depth
items.summary: Distill to Loop (Dooop) distills a pretrained non-looped diffusion transformer into a looped student with adjustable depth, initializing blocks from the teacher.
items.why: Could cut the cost of building looped diffusion transformers by reusing existing pretrained non-looped models rather than training from scratch.

items.title: Reading, Writing and Repairing Game-Theoretic Policies in Weight Space
items.summary: A study tests whether a mid-size open language model can write, read, and repair policy network weights for repeated games with exactly checkable answers.

items.title: ADE: A Zero-Training Unlearning Method for Latent World Models
items.summary: Analytical Dynamics Excision (ADE) is a deterministic, zero-training method for removing backdoor triggers and stale transitions from latent world models.
items.why: Offers a training-free unlearning approach for deployed learned simulators, avoiding the drift problems of gradient-based unlearning.

items.title: Calm Agent: Reframing Agent Interaction around Intermittent Human Attention
items.summary: Calm Agent proposes designing agents for ongoing auxiliary tasks around intermittent human attention, with Delegate, Adjust, and Check interaction modes.
items.why: Offers a design framework for agent UX where users return intermittently, relevant to teams building long-running assistants.

items.title: To Critic Or Not To Critic
items.summary: A paper examines when a learned critic improves reinforcement learning efficiency for LLMs, comparing PPO with a critic against critic-free GRPO.
items.why: Helps teams choose between PPO and GRPO for LLM RL training based on task length and complexity.

items.title: When Online Adaptation of Resilience Policies Hurts: Safe Exploration and Measurement Pitfalls in Resilience4j
items.summary: Researchers study whether an online contextual bandit can pick Resilience4j circuit breaker, retry, and bulkhead settings at runtime, finding naive adaptation sometimes underperformed defaults.
items.why: Shows that runtime tuning of microservice resilience policies can backfire without careful safe exploration and measurement, relevant to SREs considering adaptive configs.

items.title: Structure-Aware Transformers for Hierarchical Authorization in Personal AI Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose structure-aware transformers to predict users' authorization preferences for hierarchical permission requests from personal AI agents.
items.why: Could reduce permission-review burden for agent deployments, though the abstract gives little detail on results or evaluation.

items.title: HuluOPD: Unifying Heterogeneous Medical Specialists into One Lightweight Model with Unlabeled Prompts
items.summary: HuluOPD is a method that distills several heterogeneous medical specialist vision-language models into one lightweight model using only unlabeled prompts.
items.why: Offers a route to consolidate costly specialist medical VLMs into a single cheaper model without access to private training data.

items.title: Beyond Before-and-After Images: Evaluating Temporal Grounding in a Lightweight VLM for Disaster Assessment
items.summary: A diagnostic study tests whether the lightweight InternVL3-2B vision-language model truly uses pre- and post-disaster satellite images for temporal damage assessment.
items.why: Highlights that VLMs may answer change questions by relying on one image or prompt framing, a reliability concern for high-stakes remote sensing use.

items.title: Do Occupancy World Models Really Follow Actions?
items.summary: ReCast, an ego-trajectory-guided transformer, is proposed to make occupancy world models follow specified actions under counterfactual driving trajectories.
items.why: Addresses whether driving world models actually respond to action inputs, which matters for their use in planning and simulation.

items.title: Unifying Partner and Environment Diversity to Improve Human-AI Coordination
items.summary: Researchers propose a method combining partner and environment diversity to improve zero-shot human-AI coordination when both users and environments are unseen.
items.why: Targets generalization to new users and settings, a practical requirement for deployed cooperative AI, though the abstract is brief on results.

items.title: Provenance-Isolated Epistemic Quorums: Execution-Bound Evidence Certification and Plausible-World Safety Gating in Agentic Control Planes
items.summary: PIEQ, a certification layer, is presented that keeps language models outside the trusted path and gates mutating production infrastructure actions on execution-bound evidence.
items.why: Argues LLM agreement is not evidence for production changes, a design concern for teams letting agents perform incident remediation.

items.title: Spec-CoFrGeNet: Reparametrizing Continued Fraction Networks for Stable and Accurate Training
items.summary: Spec-CoFrGeNet reparametrizes continued fraction networks to improve training stability and accuracy, including for LLM training, by addressing denominator pole issues.
items.why: Shows training stability can be highly sensitive to a lower-bound choice, a practical tuning detail for this architecture class.

items.title: Integral DeltaNet: Improved Linear Attention with Adaptive Memory Integration
items.summary: Integral DeltaNet is proposed as an improved linear attention method using adaptive memory integration to reduce memory collisions in long-context modeling.
items.why: Targets a known weakness of fixed-size linear attention states for long-context language models, relevant to efficiency-focused architecture choices.

items.title: The algorithmic behavioral sink: Modeling the transition to irreversible demographic collapse
items.summary: A paper models mobile internet and AI as a synthetic mating disruptor, proposing a non-linear phase transition toward irreversible demographic collapse.

items.title: MARGIN: A Risk-Aware Agent for Robot Program Refinement
items.summary: MARGIN is a risk-aware robot-programming agent that uses a near-miss margin signal to prioritize fragile programs and guide targeted repairs.
items.why: Shows using execution-risk signals beyond binary success to refine robot control programs, relevant to robotics teams testing across unseen scenes.

items.title: Clinical3D-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Spatial Intelligence of Multimodal LLMs in Hospital Environments
items.summary: Clinical3D-Bench is a simulated benchmark with 3,368 questions on hospital-room walkthroughs to evaluate spatial intelligence of multimodal LLMs.
items.why: Provides a targeted benchmark for spatial reasoning in clinical environments, useful for teams assessing embodied or assistive models in hospitals.

items.title: PreferenceScene: Personalized Indoor Scene Synthesis from Feedback
items.summary: PreferenceScene proposes personalized indoor scene synthesis that learns hidden user preferences from multi-turn free-form feedback and satisfaction scores on rendered 3D rooms.
items.why: Demonstrates interactive preference elicitation for generative 3D content, though the abstract gives little on results.

items.title: Duo: Towards Spatiotemporal Action Coordination in Bimanual Policies
items.summary: Duo is a bimanual robot policy design that splits each arm into its own action token per timestep, enabling cross-arm attention within a shared action head.
items.why: Offers an architectural change for coordinated two-arm manipulation policies, relevant to robotics teams building flow-based policies.

items.title: An Automated Framework Integrating Deep Learning and Anatomical Reasoning for Cardiac Phenotyping From CCTA
items.summary: Researchers present an automated framework combining deep learning with anatomical reasoning to quantify pericoronary and epicardial fat from cardiac CCTA scans.
items.why: Shows how adding anatomical constraints can yield more consistent clinical measurements than segmentation alone, relevant to medical imaging pipelines.

items.title: VIDE : Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection via Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation
items.summary: VIDE proposes a training-free video anomaly detection method that estimates visual intrinsic distributions to reduce the false positives caused by anomaly bias in embedding-based approaches.
items.why: Training-free anomaly detection that adapts to each scene's normal activity could reduce false alarms without costly retraining for video surveillance systems.

items.title: Calibrated Reading of Latent Reasoning and Communication
items.summary: Researchers introduce the Calibrated Latent Reader (CLR), a compact transformer that predicts reasoning outcomes and message content from latent model states, with conformal calibration.
items.why: Offers a cheaper, more flexible way to inspect latent reasoning and key-value communication in models, aiding debugging and transparency.

items.title: RetraQ: Manifold-Constrained Critic Guidance for Flow Policies in RL
items.summary: RetraQ is a method that uses pretrained flow geometry to constrain critic-guided action gradients, aiming to keep flow-matching RL policies within data-supported regions.
items.why: Addresses critic extrapolation errors when steering flow-matching policies, which matters for teams applying offline RL to robotics or control.

items.title: Making Evaluation Explicit Is Not Enough: Supervising the Evaluation Process in Generative Reward Models
items.summary: STEP-GRM is a framework that directly supervises the intermediate evaluation steps of generative reward models, rather than only final preference outcomes.
items.why: Suggests outcome-only training can yield unsupported intermediate judgments, a concern for teams relying on LLM-as-judge evaluation pipelines.

items.title: RightDiff: Learning Generative Reward Models to Judge by the Right Differences
items.summary: RightDiff is a generative reward model that structures pairwise evaluation around response-specific differences in a single autoregressive pass to reduce shortcut exploitation.
items.why: Targets verbosity and formatting shortcuts in LLM judges, relevant for teams building reliable automated preference evaluation.

items.title: Benchmarking Protein Structure Tokenizers as Generation Targets for Language Models
items.summary: The paper benchmarks eight protein structure tokenizers by training the same 9B model to generate structure tokens, measuring how well each tokenizer can be written by a language model.
items.why: Shows reconstruction fidelity is not the property that governs generation, which matters for teams choosing tokenizers for protein language models.

items.title: Mind the Band: The Hidden Frequency Variable in Geometric RoPE
items.summary: The paper shows that unstandardized frequency bands in geometric RoPE for multi-view attention can reverse benchmark rankings, and examines this hidden variable.
items.why: Implementation defaults for positional encodings can silently change benchmark results, so teams comparing multi-view models should standardize them.

items.title: DocPristine: Content-Aware Document Appearance Enhancement under Real-World Mixed Degradations
items.summary: DocPristine is a content-aware document appearance enhancement method that targets mixed real-world degradations such as highlights, shadows, and blur in camera-captured documents.
items.why: Addresses document image cleanup under combined degradations, relevant for teams building OCR or document ingestion pipelines.

items.title: ThinkMorph-SSL: Scaling Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning with Pretext Tasks
items.summary: ThinkMorph-SSL is a two-stage training recipe that uses image pretext tasks like colorization and denoising to supervise interleaved multimodal reasoning without task-specific demonstrations.
items.why: Reduces reliance on hard-to-collect demonstrations for training models that reason through intermediate images.

items.title: Blaming the Machine, Billing the Victim? How Mock Jurors Reassign Fault from Generative AI Systems and Respond to Liability Cliffs in Tort
items.summary: A study of mock jurors examines how they reassign fault from generative AI systems to legal persons and how contributory negligence and joint liability thresholds affect findings.
items.why: Shows how liability doctrines may shape blame allocation involving AI systems, relevant for legal and risk planning for AI deployers.

items.title: SolarFilNet-V4: Multi-Scale Transformer Vision with Physics-Informed Adaptive Post-Processing for Solar Filament Segmentation
items.summary: SolarFilNet-V4 is a multi-scale transformer segmentation framework with physics-informed post-processing for segmenting solar filaments in GONG H-alpha observations.

items.title: LLM Agent Authorization Across Context Compaction
items.summary: The paper shows that request-derived authorization for LLM agents breaks during automatic context compaction, because summaries of earlier turns are placed as user messages in Claude Code and Codex.
items.why: Reveals a prompt-injection gap in agent authorization, so teams running coding agents with compaction should not assume request-based policies remain enforced.

items.title: When Answering Is Administering: Permission Replies That Rewrite Coding-Agent Policy
items.summary: The paper shows that permission replies to coding agents can rewrite the policy checked on later decisions, letting a remote service delete deny rules across a run.
items.why: Demonstrates that per-decision permission checks can fail over a whole run, a concrete risk for teams granting plugins or remote services approval rights.

items.title: Steerable by Design: Conditional Pretraining for Robust Control of Language Models
items.summary: The paper proposes a conditional pretraining method and architecture that separates instructions from data so language models are steerable by design rather than only aligned at the end.
items.why: Aims to reduce jailbreaks and in-context alignment drift by separating instruction and data channels during pretraining.

items.title: Who gets the information? An $\alpha$-fair label-coverage framework for multi-label feature selection
items.summary: FLIC is an alpha-fair label-coverage framework for multi-label feature selection that treats labels as agents whose information utility is balanced via a welfare function.
items.why: Offers a tunable fairness parameter for feature selection across labels, though its practical impact for engineering teams is limited.

items.title: OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval
items.summary: OmniEVIE is a 4.5B multi-vector embedding model covering text, images, visual documents, video, and tools, using one compressed index and a three-stage retriever.
items.why: It offers a compressed multi-vector approach to multimodal retrieval, aiming to keep local evidence while remaining cheap enough to serve at scale.

items.title: Joint Classification and Generation on Tabular Data: an Empirical Study
items.summary: Researchers present an empirical study comparing joint models that both classify and generate realistic tabular records, built from four tabular deep learning families.
items.why: It informs whether one shared model can replace two separate classifier and generator models at a given compute budget.

items.title: Roboclock: A Unified Benchmark for Time-Aware Robotic Intelligence
items.summary: Researchers introduced RoboClock, a benchmark with 60 tasks across five domains that tests time-aware robotic manipulation, including temporal constraints.
items.why: Current robotics benchmarks overlook timing constraints, so this gives teams a way to test throughput and response-time failures.

items.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Researchers propose boundary-aware policy learning to address handoff failures when an agent invokes a robot manipulation policy outside its reliable start states.
items.why: Handoff failures between agents and learned visuomotor policies are a practical reliability problem for agent-orchestrated robot systems.

items.title: CoMNO: Commutator Memory Neural Operators for Long-Horizon PDE Prediction
items.summary: Researchers present CoMNO, a Commutator Memory Neural Operator designed to reduce error accumulation in long-horizon nonlinear PDE predictions.
items.why: Neural operators that stay accurate over long horizons could make PDE simulation cheaper than traditional numerical methods.

items.title: Reproducing the Speech Labels of Qwen3-Omni's Talker: Mimi in bf16, and a Last-Frame Pitfall
items.summary: Researchers reverse-engineered the speech codec labels behind Qwen3-Omni's Talker, finding they match kyutai's Mimi codec in bf16 and documenting a calibration pitfall.
items.why: Recovering the unreleased encoder lets teams train new voices on matching labels, though the paper flags pitfalls in verification.

items.title: DAiSy: Online Data Selection by Adaptive Utility Estimation for LLM Pretraining
items.summary: Researchers introduce DAiSy, a lightweight linear auxiliary model that predicts data utility scores from frozen document embeddings for online LLM pretraining data selection.
items.why: It avoids a full forward-backward pass per candidate document, which could cut the cost of online data selection during pretraining.

items.title: Query-Guided Visual Minimization for Selective Disclosure to Cloud VLMs
items.summary: Researchers propose QGVM, a framework that locally minimizes images to disclose only query-relevant visual content before sending them to cloud vision-language models.
items.why: Teams sending images to cloud VLMs can reduce exposure of sensitive content the query does not need.

items.title: ASTERISM: Do Multimodal LLMs Actually Look at All the Images?
items.summary: An audit of about 33k items from 19 multi-image benchmarks finds that 24.2% can be answered from a single image or the question alone, a shortcut MLLMs exploit.
items.why: Benchmark scores may overstate multi-image reasoning, so teams should check whether evaluations actually require combining images.

items.title: SPRUNN: Structural Proximity for Pruning in Deep Neural Networks
items.summary: Researchers propose SPRUNN, a structural-proximity-based pruning approach for deep neural networks that aims to reduce parameters without large accuracy loss.
items.why: Pruning that preserves accuracy could make deploying compressed DNNs faster and cheaper.

items.title: When Exact Token Importance Is Not Enough: Limits of Top-K Selection in LLM Attention
items.summary: A paper shows that ranking token positions independently by exact importance and keeping the top K can fail in LLM attention, because attention weights renormalize over the chosen set.
items.why: Top-K KV cache selection heuristics may pick suboptimal token sets, which matters for long-context inference design.

items.title: A recursive self-improvement framework for electron microscopy analysis
items.summary: Researchers present PhyEvo-Mic-RSI, a physics-guided recursive self-improvement framework that turns expert corrections into reusable, versioned analysis operators for electron microscopy.
items.why: It shows a method for capturing one-off expert corrections as reusable, verifiable pipeline components in scientific analysis.

items.title: Part-Set Prototypes for Explainable Mountain Gazelles Sex Classification
items.summary: Researchers introduce set prototypes for self-explainable visual classification of mountain gazelle sex from camera-trap images.
items.why: The text gives little on broader engineering implications beyond this specific wildlife classification application.

items.title: DiCT: Teaching X-ray Vision-Language Models to Reason via Imagining CT
items.summary: Researchers propose DiCT, a three-stage framework where a CT vision-language model guides an X-ray VLM to acquire CT-informed 3D reasoning for diagnosis.

items.title: Validating Multi-Model AI-Generated Acceptance Criteria in Requirements Engineering
items.summary: A paper studies validating AI-generated acceptance criteria in requirements engineering, focusing on correctness, traceability, and hallucination in LLM-generated specifications.
items.why: Flawed AI-generated requirements can propagate into design, implementation, and verification, so validation of these artifacts matters.

items.title: Does Research-Paper Context Improve LLM-Generated Quadruped Navigation? An Exploratory Simulation Study
items.summary: Researchers test whether giving an LLM relevant research papers as context improves the navigation code it writes for a Go2 quadruped robot in simulation.
items.why: It suggests retrieving domain research may improve LLM-generated robot control code, though the abstract alone gives limited evidence of the results.

items.title: Evolve to Learn: Gradient-aligned experience evolution for model self-improvement
items.summary: Researchers propose gradient-aligned experience evolution, arguing that on-policy self-distillation should only internalize experiences that are actually worth learning for model self-improvement.
items.why: Experiences that improve test-time performance may not be worth training into weights, so teams building self-improving models need filtering.

items.title: Not All Pairs Align: Caption-Guided Audio-Visual Contrastive Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose caption-guided audio-visual contrastive learning, arguing standard objectives wrongly treat all audio-visual pairs as equally aligned despite off-screen sounds.
items.why: Standard multimodal contrastive training may learn from misaligned pairs, so pair-quality handling could matter for multimodal representation training.

items.title: Verify then Steer: Progress Hallucination-Aware Recovery for Continuous Vision-and-Language Navigation
items.summary: Researchers identify progress hallucination in vision-and-language navigation, where agents mistake off-route observations for task progress, and propose a verify-then-steer recovery method.
items.why: Agents that misjudge task progress after route deviations can fail to recover, a reliability issue for embodied AI deployments.

items.title: CPU-Eval: Evaluating Large Language Models for CPU Hardware Code Generation
items.summary: Researchers introduce CPU-Eval, a benchmark of 339 hardware description language generation problems drawn from six CPU designs, to test LLMs beyond saturated VerilogEval.
items.why: Hardware code generation teams get a harder benchmark, since leading systems already exceed 90% pass rates on VerilogEval.

items.title: BEACON: Learning Observation-Conditioned Starting Points for Guided Conditional Flow Matching in Microscopy
items.summary: Researchers present BEACON, which learns observation-conditioned starting points for guided conditional flow matching to restore degraded fluorescence microscopy images.
items.why: It offers a method for computational microscopy restoration that aims to preserve biologically meaningful structures while enabling lower light dose imaging.

items.title: Within-task hazards of AI agents: unidentified by time-horizon curves, identified by repeated runs
items.summary: A paper argues that AI agent time-horizon curves cannot show whether failure hazard declines within a task, and that repeated runs are needed to identify within-task hazards.
items.why: Teams relying on time-horizon curves to judge agent reliability may draw wrong conclusions about failure patterns; repeated-run data is needed.

items.title: NRG-Twins: Pixel-Level Ground Truth for Rigidity Violations in Generated Videos
items.summary: Researchers present NRG-Twins, a method providing pixel-level ground-truth labels for rigidity violations in generated videos, to help make video generators more 3D consistent.
items.why: Generated video often deforms static content, and per-pixel labels could support training rewards or guidance for more 3D-consistent generators.

items.title: See the Answer, Learn to Embed: Learning Universal Multimodal Embeddings from Hindsight
items.summary: Researchers propose learning universal multimodal embeddings by letting models see the matched candidate during training, avoiding extra inference-time reasoning computation.
items.why: Training with hindsight context could yield embedding models that avoid the added inference cost of reasoning-driven approaches.

items.title: Describe, Don't Ask: Caption-Driven On-Policy Distillation for Fine-Grained Visual Perception
items.summary: Researchers propose caption-driven on-policy distillation to improve vision-language models' fine-grained perception, reducing reliance on costly region-specific question-answer curation.
items.why: Replacing per-region QA curation with captions could make fine-grained visual distillation easier to scale for multimodal training pipelines.

items.title: Gamification in the age of AI: surveying player perceptions of motivation, manipulation, and data protection
items.summary: A survey of 28 adults finds players are concerned about manipulation, personal data collection, and transparency in AI-driven gamification.
items.why: Small survey of player attitudes; relevant mainly to teams designing engagement features that use user modeling and personal data.

items.title: Progressive Reliable Supervision for Black-Box Universal Domain Adaptation
items.summary: Researchers propose Progressive Reliable Supervision (PReS) for black-box universal domain adaptation, where neither source data nor source-model parameters are accessible.
items.why: Adapting models without source data or parameters addresses a restrictive deployment setting, though the abstract offers limited detail on results.

items.title: CodeWAM: A Code World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Researchers propose CodeWAM, a driving world model that represents ego vehicle dynamics as executable code alongside a learned visual model for end-to-end autonomous driving.
items.why: Combining executable code with learned visual models for driving planning is an architectural idea engineers in autonomy may evaluate.

items.title: Assessing Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Deep Reinforcement Learning for Cyber-Physical Systems
items.summary: Researchers evaluate how robust three classes of reinforcement learning algorithms are to catastrophic forgetting in continual learning for cyber-physical systems.
items.why: Forgetting previously learned behaviours threatens safety in deployed RL controllers that must adapt to changing environments.

items.title: Branch and Consolidate: A Unified Recipe for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: Researchers present a unified multimodal multi-teacher on-policy distillation recipe that consolidates specialists which diverge substantially from a shared checkpoint back into one student.
items.why: Existing merging and distillation methods reportedly struggle when specialists drift far from the base checkpoint, relevant to multi-model consolidation work.

items.title: Wi-Fi Enabled Edge Intelligence Framework for Smart City Traffic Monitoring using Low-Power IoT Cameras
items.summary: Researchers propose a localized edge AI framework connecting low-power IoT cameras to a client or NVIDIA Jetson Nano over Wi-Fi for smart city traffic monitoring.
items.why: Shows a low-latency edge inference design that avoids cloud round trips for time-critical tasks like incident detection and congestion management.

items.title: ContinualDrive: A Deployment-Anchored, Multi-Axis Benchmark for Continual Updates of Learned Driving Planners
items.summary: ContinualDrive is a benchmark for post-deployment continual updates of learned driving planners, using real nuPlan logs and open and closed loop evaluation.
items.why: Gives teams a way to test whether updating a deployed driving planner actually improves on the current model.

items.title: Next-Manip: On-Demand Agent-Policy Collaboration for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Next-Manip proposes on-demand collaboration between multimodal agents and learned policies for robotic manipulation, switching between them as needed.
items.why: Suggests a hybrid design where expensive reasoning agents are called only when a fast control policy fails.

items.title: MXI-MemICL: Towards In-Context Robot Manipulation through Self-Retrieved Interaction Memory
items.summary: MXI-MemICL introduces memory-guided in-context learning for vision-language-action models, treating robot demonstrations as retrievable memory to learn new manipulation skills.
items.why: Offers a way to teach robots new skills from a single demonstration without parameter updates or extra annotations.

items.title: Boiling Down Uncertainty: Deep Generative Scenario Search with Decision-Guided Evolution Strategies for Two-Stage Stochastic Optimization
items.summary: Researchers derive analytical gradients for Deep Generative Scenario Search, a method that generates and refines scenarios for two-stage stochastic optimization.
items.why: Provides a theoretical foundation for a scenario generation method, which may improve decision quality under uncertainty.

items.title: Gated Concept Adapters: Layer-Wise Concept Bottlenecks for Auditable Text Understanding
items.summary: Gated Concept Adapters add layer-wise, low-dimensional concept bottlenecks to pretrained Transformers to make text understanding predictions more inspectable and auditable.
items.why: Offers a route to auditable intervention points in models used for moderation and other sensitive text decisions.

items.title: RoboRecast: Intent-Preserving Demonstration Augmentation via Diagnosis-Driven Optimization
items.summary: RoboRecast is an agentic optimization framework that augments robot demonstrations in simulation by jointly adjusting scene and robot motion while preserving task interactions.
items.why: Could reduce the cost of collecting real-world manipulation demonstrations for robot policy learning.

items.title: REBEAL: Human References Are No Longer the Best Translation, and Metrics Do Not Notice
items.summary: REBEAL is a benchmark testing how machine translation metrics respond to controlled flaws in human reference translations, noting references contain annotated errors.
items.why: Shows reference-based MT metrics may be unreliable when references are flawed, affecting how teams evaluate translation systems.

items.title: MargEmbed-Akan: Bridging Twi Questions and English Knowledge through Cross-Lingual Score Distillation
items.summary: The MargEmbed-Akan paper evaluates eight retrieval systems on Twi-English cross-lingual tasks and introduces a distilled embedding model for Twi questions.
items.why: Highlights gaps in embedding retrieval for low-resource languages like Twi, relevant to multilingual search builders.

items.title: ReFocus: Progress-Guided Adaptive Practice for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: ReFocus is a progress-guided multi-round reinforcement learning framework that alternates global and local RL to find and practice bottlenecks in long-horizon robotic manipulation.
items.why: Addresses sparse feedback in long-horizon robot RL by targeting specific bottleneck stages for practice.

items.title: BARE: Body-Aware Reflexive Evasion for Humanoid Robots
items.summary: BARE proposes body-aware reflexive evasion for humanoid robots, using small localized body adjustments to dodge rapidly approaching obstacles.

items.title: TeamFlowRL: Online Policy Optimization of Decentralized Flow Policies for Multi-Agent Coordination
items.summary: TeamFlowRL pretrains multi-agent flow policies offline and fine-tunes them online with reinforcement learning for cooperative multi-agent coordination.
items.why: Offers a method for improving generative multi-agent policies beyond fixed datasets through online interaction.

items.title: ICLWorld: Benchmarking In-Context Learning of Agents from Digital to Physical Worlds
items.summary: ICLWorld is an online benchmark that evaluates in-context learning of agents across computer use and robot control in digital and physical settings.
items.why: Provides a contamination-resistant way to assess whether agents adapt to new rules at inference time across computers and robots.

items.title: DexWAC: A Unified World-Actor-Critic Model for Dexterous Robot Manipulation
items.summary: DexWAC is a unified world-actor-critic model for dexterous robot manipulation that combines action prediction, dynamics, and value learning in one model.
items.why: Suggests sharing representations across world modeling and policy learning could reduce training overhead for robot policies.

items.title: Bathys: Advancing Deep Search Agents
items.summary: Bathys 9B and 27B are deep search agents trained with verifiable question synthesis, post-training, and online RL under context compression.
items.why: Describes a training pipeline for multi-step search agents that gather evidence iteratively and verify answers.

items.title: Are We Rewarding the Wrong Module? Module-Specific Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose Module-Specific Policy Optimization to stop RLVR/GRPO from applying one advantage signal to all modules of multimodal LLMs, including the vision encoder, projector, and LLM.
items.why: It targets credit-assignment flaws in RL fine-tuning of multimodal models, which could affect how teams train vision-language reasoning systems.

items.title: FourStat: A Dual AutoEncoder Leveraging Frequency and Stationarity for Time Series Anomaly Detection
items.summary: FourStat is a dual autoencoder for univariate time series anomaly detection, combining a Fourier autoencoder for global patterns with a stationary autoencoder for local structure.
items.why: Univariate anomaly detection is a common monitoring need, and the approach claims to address settings where many existing methods perform poorly.

items.title: ASCENT: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Advancing Stepwise Diagnostic Reasoning in Large Language Models on Common Clinical Scenarios
items.summary: ASCENT is a clinician-annotated benchmark of 3,078 stepwise diagnostic problems derived from MedQA-USMLE, designed to evaluate how LLMs revise impressions as clinical information accumulates.
items.why: It offers a way to test LLMs on multi-step clinical reasoning rather than only final answers, relevant to healthcare AI evaluation.

items.title: ReQOR: Operator-Discrepancy Subspace Repair for Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors in Large Language Models
items.summary: ReQOR proposes a method to repair quantization-conditioned backdoors in LLMs, which behave maliciously only after quantization while appearing benign at high precision.
items.why: Teams that quantize models for deployment may need to verify quantized versions, since backdoors can appear only after compression.

items.title: SGD with Large Learning Rates: General Analysis & Improved Rates
items.summary: Researchers analyze stochastic gradient descent with large learning rates and report improved convergence rates, answering an open question about whether large-stepsize benefits persist under gradient noise.
items.why: Results on stepsize choice under noise could inform optimizer tuning, though the text gives limited practical detail.

items.title: C3H: Compression-to-Consensus Criteria Hijacking in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems
items.summary: The C3H paper shows that compression and cross-modal fusion in multimodal LLM recommenders can expose a compression-to-consensus bias that attackers can exploit to hijack ranking decisions.
items.why: Recommender systems built on multimodal LLMs may be vulnerable to content manipulation that exploits the same mechanisms meant to add robustness.

items.title: Scaling Laws of Ensemble Uncertainty in Language Models
items.summary: Researchers argue that existing Bayesian deep learning methods miss much of LLM epistemic uncertainty and study how ensemble uncertainty scales with model size.
items.why: Reliable uncertainty estimates matter for safety and exploration use cases, and the scaling analysis may inform how teams estimate model confidence.

items.title: Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep
items.summary: Researchers propose a sleep-like process in which a model runs recurrent forward passes over context to turn a few in-context examples into generalizable knowledge, improving sample efficiency.
items.why: If effective, a sleep-style refinement step could help models learn from limited user interactions or unfamiliar code without retraining.

items.title: MRBench: Benchmarking Physical Necessity Reasoning in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Manipulation
items.summary: MRBench is a benchmark for physical necessity reasoning in heterogeneous multi-robot manipulation, testing which robots are truly needed for a task as capabilities and resources change.
items.why: It highlights that successful robot coordination does not show which team members are required, a gap for planning in multi-robot systems.

items.title: Residual Guidance for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
items.summary: Researchers identify context inertia in streaming video generation, where models keep following the previous prompt after a switch, and propose residual guidance to address it.
items.why: Interactive video tools that let users change prompts mid-generation face this lag, which affects responsiveness in real-time products.

items.title: Reliable and grounded reporting of any computed tomography scan with FORA
items.summary: FORA is a general-purpose CT model that localizes 1,028 radiological concepts and generates reports across 28 CT protocols, trained on 304,962 routine CT examinations.
items.why: It suggests a broader, spatially grounded approach to radiology AI than models limited to specific organs or predefined abnormalities.

items.title: Field Life: Particle Life as Interacting Chemical Fields
items.summary: Field Life is a cellular automaton inspired by Particle Life, where each colour is a channel holding concentrations per cell and interactions follow a ring-kernel convolution and interaction matrix.
items.why: It is a research artifact on emergent dynamics with limited direct relevance to engineering or business decisions.

items.title: Path-probability gradients for optimizing force fields against dynamical observables
items.summary: PathGrad introduces path-probability gradients for refining machine learning force fields against dynamical observables by differentiating Langevin path probabilities instead of chaotic trajectories.
items.why: It offers a route to fit simulation models to experimental dynamics, relevant mainly to computational chemistry and materials teams.

items.title: MXFP4 for LLM Inference: Complementary Post-Training Quantization Techniques and Their Interactions
items.summary: A study of six LLMs and three microscaling formats (including MXFP6 and MXFP4) examines how post-training quantization techniques compose and interact.
items.why: Practical guidance on combining MXFP4 with rotation and scale selection can inform low-precision LLM inference deployments.

items.title: Adaptive Electromagnetic Transient-level Digital Twins for Data Centers via In-Context Learning with LLMs
items.summary: Researchers propose adaptive electromagnetic transient-level digital twins for data centers using in-context learning with LLMs to speed up transient prediction versus high-fidelity solvers.
items.why: Faster transient simulation could help data center operators plan for AI-driven power demand swings, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Joint Detection of Constructive Speech, Hate Speech and Agreement in Online Conversations
items.summary: Researchers collected and annotated a large English and Danish dataset for jointly detecting constructive speech, hate speech, and agreement in online conversations.
items.why: Offers training data and methods for automated moderation that promotes constructive counter-speech, useful for trust and safety teams building classifiers.

items.title: Motion Conditioned World Modeling for Embodied Visual Tracking
items.summary: Researchers propose Motion-Conditioned World Modeling, which feeds predicted target motion and robot ego-motion into latent state transitions for embodied visual tracking.
items.why: Shows how modeling target motion and viewpoint changes in world models can improve prediction for robots that track moving objects.

items.title: Efficient Video Retrieval Augmented Generation via Token Allocation
items.summary: Researchers introduce Lembas, a plug-and-play framework that treats video retrieval-augmented generation as a token allocation problem across frames and subtitles under a shared budget.
items.why: Could reduce VLM token costs for long-video understanding by allocating a fixed token budget more efficiently across retrieved content.

items.title: Do Vision-Language Models Know Their Own Visual Weaknesses? Probing Capability-Level Metacognition
items.summary: A study finds vision-language models poorly predict in advance which visual tasks and image conditions are hard for them, across open and proprietary models.
items.why: Suggests teams cannot rely on VLMs to self-report their weak spots, so external capability testing remains necessary before deployment.

items.title: "I Do Intend to Deliver": Will LLMs Run a Marketplace Advance-Fee Scam?
items.summary: Researchers prompted ten off-the-shelf LLMs to play sellers in a marketplace advance-fee scam across 1,200 simulated buyer conversations, without jailbreaks.
