items.why: Highlights that hosted LLMs may be usable for scalable fraud with simple prompts, a concern for platform abuse and safety controls.

items.title: Attestation is All You Need: Toward a Zero-Trust Architecture for HPC AI Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose AEGIS, a runtime behavioral attestation system to defend HPC AI agents against hijacking via prompt injection, poisoned data, or compromised tools.
items.why: Addresses a security gap where authorized agents can exfiltrate data through legitimate encrypted LLM API traffic that existing cluster defenses miss.

items.title: Benchmarking Evidence Sufficiency in Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Researchers released DriveAnswer, a benchmark of 20,151 questions testing whether driving vision-language models judge if visual evidence is sufficient to answer.
items.why: Separates grounding from answerability, helping teams tell well-supported autonomous driving predictions from ones based on insufficient evidence.

items.title: CAPER: PartGround and PlanRefine for Reliable Manual-Guided Robotic Assembly Planning
items.summary: Researchers propose CAPER, a framework with PartGround and PlanRefine modules to help VLMs generate robotic assembly procedures from manuals with accurate part identities.
items.why: Targets reliability issues like unsupported part IDs in VLM-based robot planning, relevant to teams automating assembly workflows.

items.title: On Potentiality and Actuality Of Foundation Models
items.summary: Researchers decompose foundation model adaptations into a shared input-independent component and a residual, finding the shared part accounts for most adaptation gains.
items.why: Suggests much of fine-tuning gain may come from a simple learnable shift, potentially enabling cheaper adaptation methods.

items.title: One, No One and One Hundred Thousand CTs: Testing Anatomical Control in Text-to-CT Generation
items.summary: Researchers introduce CtrlCT, a toolkit that standardizes evaluation of text-to-CT generators and tests whether report edits consistently change the generated anatomy.
items.why: Provides a common evaluation protocol for medical text-to-CT generators, though the source text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: LEGOSpec: A Composable and Efficient Framework for Speculative Draft Design and Training
items.summary: Researchers present LEGOSpec, a composable framework that decomposes speculative decoding draft models into Context, Backbone, Proposal, and Objective components for systematic study.
items.why: Helps engineers understand how individual draft-model design choices affect speculative decoding speed, though specific results are not in the provided text.

items.title: Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test: How a Simple Mirror Breaks Robot Policies
items.summary: Researchers introduce RoboDojo-Mirror, a benchmark showing that adding mirrors to scenes causes five robot manipulation policies to perform worse.
items.why: Reveals that common robot policies are brittle to reflections, a failure mode teams should test before deploying manipulation systems.

items.title: Can a Frontier LLM Repair a Quantized Network by Tool-Free Weight-Space Programming?
items.summary: Researchers tested whether four Claude-family LLMs could convert a CIFAR-10 CNN's weights to a 4-bit network without tools, where round-to-nearest quantization drops accuracy from 81.4% to 60.4%.
items.why: Probes the limits of LLMs reasoning directly over model weights, a question relevant to quantization and model compression workflows.

items.title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to US industrial might — not a champion
items.summary: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld argues that Jensen Huang's White House-backed return as Nvidia CEO and board member could be a mistake, exposing directors to lawsuits.
items.why: It flags governance and legal risk for leadership and boards, and questions Nvidia's role in US chip policy and export concerns.

items.title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy
items.summary: Jensen Huang reportedly still opposes a succession plan at Nvidia, arguing it would create unnecessary hierarchy, after the company's recent leadership disruption.

items.title: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
items.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang apologized to staff at an all-hands meeting, thanked the White House, and said he is in therapy.

items.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
items.summary: A new benchmark finds that even the most advanced AI models struggle to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely, sometimes introducing new problems.
items.why: Engineers building personal assistant agents should expect unreliable task completion and new safety failure modes in real-world use.

items.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
items.summary: Walmart now lets customers shop Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta's AI agent.
items.why: It shows a major retailer integrating with a third-party AI agent platform, a distribution channel for agentic commerce.

items.title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself
items.summary: Maple raised $5.3M to build AI products with encrypted architecture designed to keep even the company from accessing user data.
items.why: Its design aims to make private data inaccessible to the provider, a privacy-by-architecture approach relevant to teams handling sensitive data.

items.title: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, in his first all-hands since returning, apologized to staff and denied that Trump or tech leaders helped him get his job back.
items.why: Leadership turmoil at a key AI chip supplier can affect supply, roadmap, and partner confidence.

items.title: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups
items.summary: Anthropic's shares have fallen below its IPO price, raising concerns about valuations across AI startups.
items.why: A weak post-IPO debut for a leading AI lab could tighten funding and valuation expectations for AI companies.

items.title: David Fincher is being dragged for suspected use of AI in his latest film
items.summary: Early screenings of David Fincher's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel have prompted viewers to suspect generative AI was used in the film.
items.why: Reports cite uncanny, inconsistent visuals, highlighting ongoing questions about undisclosed AI use in media production.

items.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
items.summary: The UK's cyber agency warns that AI hacking tools are exploiting simple, long-standing security flaws, urging stronger foundations.
items.why: Engineering teams should prioritize basic security hygiene, since AI-driven attacks are targeting known weaknesses.

items.title: Meta brings its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs
items.summary: Meta has integrated its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs, so users no longer need to switch to the separate Muse app.
items.why: Embedding AI agents in existing messaging flows shows how assistants are moving into the apps people already use.

items.title: Microduck Obstacle Avoidance: A Sim2Real Workflow with Isaac Lab and Newton
items.summary: Hugging Face published a tutorial on a sim-to-real workflow for obstacle avoidance on a Microduck robot using Isaac Lab and Newton.

items.title: Jensen Huang deepfakes are the hot new AI slop
items.summary: Viral AI-generated deepfake videos of Nvidia's Jensen Huang, including one with nearly 6 million Instagram views, are spreading online.
items.why: Realistic deepfakes of executives raise impersonation and misinformation risks for companies and their leaders.

items.title: Tidal bans AI-generated music
items.summary: Streaming service Tidal has banned AI-generated music from its platform, according to a Variety report.
items.why: Platform content policies on AI-generated media are tightening, which affects distributors and creators building on music services.

items.title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
items.summary: An investor in Crusoe argues that solar and energy storage are the obvious power choice for future AI data centers needing tens of gigawatts.
items.why: Power supply is becoming a central constraint for AI infrastructure planning, pushing toward renewables and storage.

items.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
items.summary: The New York Times has told freelance photographers not to update to the 2027 version of Adobe Photoshop, citing AI features that may not be apparent to users.
items.why: Hidden AI features in creative software can create compliance and provenance problems for professional workflows.

items.title: Pinterest will now let parents limit the AI-generated content their teens see
items.summary: Pinterest will let parents limit the AI-generated content their teens see in their feeds.
items.why: Platforms are adding user controls over AI-generated content, which may shape future content-labeling and filtering requirements.

items.title: How Gemini is changing the game for Golden State's organization and fans.
items.summary: Google says Gemini is partnering with the Golden State Warriors, Valkyries, and Chase Center to power fan experiences and business operations.

items.title: Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia
items.summary: Amazon is reportedly acquiring Decart for $7.5 billion as part of efforts to make its Trainium chips more efficient.
items.why: Software-driven efficiency gains could help close the performance gap between custom AI chips and Nvidia's hardware.

items.title: Raising the stakes for enterprise networks with AI modernization
items.summary: An MIT Technology Review sponsored piece says agentic AI is adding heavy load to enterprise networks, with agent tasks generating an estimated 450% more traffic than human work.
items.why: Agentic AI workloads could substantially increase network traffic, so enterprise networks need modernization planning.

items.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
items.summary: OpenAI reports GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code, with lab tests showing binding across five targets.

items.title: LLM agents work for their parent companies, not for you
items.summary: A Hacker News-linked essay argues that LLM agents work for their parent companies rather than for the users they interact with.
items.why: Engineers deploying agents should consider whose interests agents are built to serve, especially for user-facing products.

items.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
items.summary: Amazon reports that hackers used AI agents, built on the Cairn framework, to find and exploit a zero-day vulnerability with little human involvement.
items.why: Shows attackers can automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation, raising the urgency for defenders to adopt similar AI-driven security tooling.

items.title: Searching for distant planets with Astra
items.summary: OpenAI describes two amateur astronomers using Codex and Astra to search public NASA Kepler and TESS data for potential exoplanets.

items.title: Jevons Paradox in AI: Cheaper Tokens Won't Pay for Capex
items.summary: A Hacker News post argues that cheaper AI tokens will not generate enough revenue to pay back the capital expenditure behind AI infrastructure.
items.why: Leaders planning AI budgets should question whether falling per-token prices can offset large infrastructure investments, as the cited argument suggests they may not.

items.title: Introducing the Amazon Bedrock Trusted Access API with Anthropic’s Enterprise Frontier Safeguards and Enterprise Data Controls
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock launched a Trusted Access API to discover, request, and enroll in model provider programs, with Anthropic's EFS and EDC offerings in public preview.
items.why: Engineers using Claude models on Bedrock gain a single path to request data controls and safeguards, though the text gives no detail on terms or availability.

items.title: SAMA: Training-Free Consensus Ridge Tracking for Camera-Based Heart Rate on Five Public Datasets
items.summary: Researchers introduced SAMA, a training-free method for camera-based heart rate estimation, evaluated on five public datasets with short-window tracking.
items.why: Engineers building remote health monitoring can see a benchmark focused on short windows, which matters for tele-consultation use; the text gives few further specifics.

items.title: torchtsetlin: Fast, Interpretable Tsetlin Machines for PyTorch
items.summary: Researchers released torchtsetlin, a PyTorch implementation of Tsetlin machines covering several variants, including convolutional and segmentation models.
items.why: Teams wanting interpretable rule-based models could use these as standard PyTorch modules instead of separate C and CUDA wrappers.

items.title: From Point Clouds to Engineering Models: Benchmarking Agentic 3D Reconstruction in the Built Environment
items.summary: Researchers introduced S2Bench, a benchmark of 128 real-world scenes for agentic scan-to-BIM 3D reconstruction of built environments.
items.why: Engineers working on agents that turn scans into CAD or BIM models get a benchmark with expert reference models, though the text gives limited results.

items.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
items.summary: Researchers proposed AutoPILOT, a visual agent harness that lets a model issue primitive actions or start ongoing operations, aiming at real-time gameplay.
items.why: The harness design targets a gap where models fail when games keep running, which is relevant to building real-time agents; the text offers few results.

items.title: FinEvo: Recursive Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Financial Modeling
items.summary: Researchers introduced FinEvo, a self-evolution framework that aims to improve LLMs' long-horizon financial modeling through autonomous experience construction.
items.why: Teams building financial AI may find the self-improvement loop relevant, but the text does not report outcomes.

items.title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
items.summary: Researchers studied how context and skill management in harnesses affect self-evolving autoresearch agents that design and run experiments.
items.why: Engineers building long-running research agents get a systematic look at which harness components actually drive performance.

items.title: A Nepali-Accented English Evaluation Dataset for Automatic Speech Recognition
items.summary: Researchers released a Nepali-accented English evaluation dataset for benchmarking automatic speech recognition under accent mismatch.
items.why: Teams deploying ASR for South Asian users can use this dataset to measure accuracy on an under-served accent.

items.title: Temporal Logic Tensor Networks: Foundations of Temporal Reasoning in Neural Networks
items.summary: Researchers presented Temporal Logic Tensor Networks, a neural approach for reasoning over events at different time scales in dynamic scenes.
items.why: The text is mostly framing; it offers little concrete detail for engineers beyond the motivation.

items.title: Specialized Large Language Models for Markovian Reasoning: Structural Cache Compression, Transition Pretraining, and Dual-Loop Transformers
items.summary: Researchers proposed specialized Markovian-reasoning LLMs using structural KV cache compression, transition pretraining, and dual-loop transformers.
items.why: Reducing KV cache memory and throughput bottlenecks in long-chain reasoning is directly relevant to inference cost, though results are not given here.

items.title: Feedback-Driven Prompt Refinement for Educational AI: Affective Trajectory Estimation and Bloom's Taxonomy Classification
items.summary: Researchers showed that feedback-driven prompt refinement with affective and cognitive signals improves educational AI classification without updating model parameters.
items.why: Teams building educational tools can improve reliability through prompt refinement alone, without fine-tuning the executor model.

items.title: GERF: A Token-Efficient Multimodal Retrieval Framework for Schema-Guided Scientific Information Extraction
items.summary: Researchers introduced GERF, a token-efficient multimodal retrieval framework for schema-guided extraction of experimental details from scientific papers.
items.why: Pipelines extracting data from text, tables, and figures may benefit from its token-efficient retrieval, though the text gives no benchmark figures.

items.title: INSEP: Refusal-Direction Inseparability as a Defense Against Abliteration
items.summary: Researchers proposed INSEP, a defense against abliteration attacks that fine-tunes LLMs to reduce separability of harmful and benign activations along the refusal direction.
items.why: Teams hardening open-weight LLMs against safety-removal attacks get a candidate defense, though its effectiveness is not detailed here.

items.title: Selection Policies for Equal-Byte Mixed-Precision Quantization of Small Language Models
items.summary: Researchers compared parent-selection rules in a genetic algorithm for allocating 2, 4, or 8 bits across matrices in small language models under equal byte budgets.
items.why: Engineers compressing small models on fixed storage budgets get a comparison of mixed-precision allocation search strategies.

items.title: MatHarness: Towards Long-Horizon Open-ended AutoResearch for Computational Materials Science
items.summary: Researchers introduced MatHarness, an agent harness for open-ended, long-horizon computational materials research from ideation to manuscript writing.
items.why: Teams building research agents for scientific domains can study its pre-flight verification and skill-distillation design, though results are not in the text.

items.title: Decision models for UAVBench and the viability of edge deployment
items.summary: Researchers study whether small structured decision models can run on drone edge computers, using the UAVBench benchmark and a Mac for initial screening.
items.why: It addresses whether benchmark scores predict real onboard deployment, relevant to engineers planning edge AI on resource-limited hardware.

items.title: When Tools Fail, Agents Fabricate: Silent Failure and Verification-First Oversight in Tool-Using LLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers test how LLM agents fail when tools break, across 2,100 fault-injected runs, finding agents may fabricate results instead of reporting failures.
items.why: Silent fabrication after tool failures is a reliability risk for anyone deploying tool-using agents, pointing to verification-first oversight.

items.title: SMAD: A Semantics-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Unsupervised Time-Series Anomaly Detection
items.summary: SMAD is an LLM-based multi-agent framework that turns anomaly intent into executable time-series anomaly detection pipelines without supervision.

items.title: Engram: Multi-Stage Memory for Agentic Tuning of Heterogeneous Models
items.summary: Engram is a memory system that lets LLM agents reuse past neural network tuning trial outcomes across sessions and heterogeneous models.
items.why: Cross-session memory could cut costly repeated trials when agents tune production models, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Schedule, Rank, Profile: Continuous Evaluation of LLM Agents in Games
items.summary: Researchers propose a framework for continuous evaluation of LLM agents in games, scheduling matchups and ranking models to avoid costly full round-robin testing.
items.why: Continuous, scalable agent evaluation helps teams keep benchmarks current as models and prompts change.

items.title: CausalNTP: A World-Model Recipe for Causal Next-Token Prediction under Noisy Training-data
items.summary: The paper shows transformers trained with next-token prediction fail to rely only on causally relevant left-context tokens, and proposes a causal world-model recipe to fix this.
items.why: It identifies a training deficiency in next-token prediction that could affect reliability of models trained on noisy data.

items.title: The Effect of Security-Focused Prompts on Reported Findings: A Controlled Experiment on 400 AI-Generated Web Applications
items.summary: A controlled experiment on 400 AI-generated web apps compares security outcomes when OWASP-aligned security prompts are appended, across Claude Code and Codex CLI.
items.why: Agentic coding tools' default security posture matters for teams shipping generated apps, and prompt-level security requirements may change it.

items.title: Diversity over Scale: Recursive Self-Improvement with Ensembles of Small Open-Weight Models
items.summary: DiVE is an ensemble method for recursive self-improvement that uses diverse small open-weight models to rewrite programs instead of relying on frontier models.
items.why: Using cheaper small open-weight model ensembles could make self-improvement loops less expensive and less prone to stalling.

items.title: Human-in-the-Loop Runbook Improvement with Agentic Support Automation
items.summary: Researchers present an agentic support automation approach that keeps operational runbooks improved with human-in-the-loop review for production service support.
items.why: Keeping runbooks current with agent help could reduce operator response times for production software teams.

items.title: ESM-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Whether AI Agents Understand Earth System Model Physics and Code
items.summary: ESM-Bench introduces 60 developer-commit tasks from six Earth System Model repositories to test whether AI coding agents preserve physical assumptions in code.
items.why: Agents editing scientific code must keep both software interfaces and physics intact, and this benchmark tests that directly.

items.title: Walks2Maps: Learning Indoor Geometry from Crowdsourced Wi-Fi RTT and Motion Trajectories
items.summary: Walks2Maps reconstructs indoor floor-plan geometry from crowdsourced smartphone walks and Wi-Fi round-trip-time measurements, without surveyed access-point coordinates.
items.why: Crowdsourced indoor mapping without floor plans or surveyed positions could lower the cost of building indoor location maps.

items.title: X-AQA: Unifying Action Quality Assessment with Multimodal Large Language Models and Multi-Domain Learning
items.summary: X-AQA is a unified training and evaluation framework for action quality assessment using multimodal LLMs, trained on a 40,163-sample corpus across four domains.

items.title: From atomic events to material degradation across metre and year scales
items.summary: Researchers propose a method linking atomic-scale events to material degradation over metre and year scales, beyond what engineering simulations usually reach.

items.title: Beyond Unit Tests: Path-Aware Rubric-Guided LLM Autograding of Notebooks
items.summary: An LLM-based autograder generates rubrics that evaluate multi-step Jupyter notebook assessments by considering the path a student took through interdependent steps.
items.why: Path-aware LLM grading offers a way to assess open-ended, flow-structured work that unit tests cannot judge.

items.title: EvoViM: Recursively Self-Evolving Visual Agents for Exploration with Deferred Queries
items.summary: EvoViM is a self-evolving framework where a frozen multimodal model converts its interaction experience into a visual program that retains images and computes on pixels.
items.why: Storing visual evidence and computing on pixels for deferred queries could inform how teams design memory for multimodal agents.

items.title: Agent Money Benchmark: Can AI Agents Be Trusted to Spend Money?
items.summary: Researchers introduced Agent Money Benchmark, testing 12 models on whether AI agents spend a client's money well on information purchases paid in USDC via x402.
items.why: Agents with wallets buying data raise spending-control and trust questions that engineers deploying payment-enabled agents must measure.

items.title: Internalized Experience: How Training Data Shapes Memory Formation in LLMs
items.summary: Researchers introduced FSMem, a state-transition framework for building training data and studying how data shapes LLM parametric memory of reusable task rules.
items.why: It suggests training data organization affects whether models internalize reusable rules, relevant to teams designing fine-tuning datasets.

items.title: VeriLadder: A Multi-Agent Specification Refinement System for Tool-Verified Verilog Datasets
items.summary: VeriLadder is a five-level Verilog dataset built by a multi-agent framework where LLM agents write specifications and EDA tools decide acceptance.
items.why: Tool-verified dataset generation addresses the scarcity of correct RTL training data for LLMs writing hardware code.

items.title: Distilling Visual Agents from Limited Interaction Experience
items.summary: Researchers study how little interaction experience is needed to distill a capable visual agent, using selected trajectories and on-policy distillation across Navigation and Sokoban.
items.why: Findings suggest a small number of trajectories can transfer, which may lower data costs for training visual agents.

items.title: Mitigating Backdoors in Masked Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Researchers present UNMASK, described as the first defense against backdoor attacks on masked diffusion language models, which are vulnerable to trigger-based malicious outputs.
items.why: Teams adopting diffusion language models need defenses against backdoors that cause targeted malicious generation.

items.title: Unlearning Model Identity: Ablating LoRA Weights from Question-Based Identity Tuning
items.summary: Researchers study removing proprietary model identity from open-weight LLMs by ablating LoRA weights tied to question-based identity tuning.
items.why: Providers customizing open-weight models for downstream products need reliable ways to remove inherited vendor identity traits.

items.title: Persuasion from Within: Model-Based Insider Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Debate and Consensus
items.summary: Researchers study model-based insider attacks where a malicious agent joins a multi-agent LLM debate or consensus and persuades others toward a hidden goal.
items.why: Multi-agent systems that assume all participants share objectives may be vulnerable to covert persuasion, a risk for collective-decision deployments.

items.title: Improving the Improver: Semantic PID Control for Medical Agent Self-Improvement
items.summary: Researchers propose semantic PID control to improve recursive self-improvement of medical agents, applied to CliAgent for pathological staging and survival prediction tasks.

items.title: DeCo: Decoupled Traffic State Modeling with Cross-Variable Coordination
items.summary: DeCo is a decoupled traffic state modeling framework that forecasts traffic flow, occupancy, and speed with cross-variable coordination.

items.title: Can Your AI Twin Meet People for You? It Can Hold a Conversation. But What Does It Need to Judge Like You?
items.summary: Researchers built LLM twins of 710 CANDOR participants and tested whether simulated first conversations predict real liking, reporting a correlation of 0.277.
items.why: Simulated persona rehearsals showing predictive signal could inform how agents act on users' behalf, though the reported effect is modest.

items.title: Beyond Single-Turn Privacy: Training-Data Leakage in Conversational RAG
items.summary: Researchers introduce CRELT, a framework that tracks turn-by-turn leakage of real contact details from training data in conversational RAG systems.
items.why: Multi-turn conversations may leak personal data even when single-turn RAG appears protected, a concern for privacy-sensitive deployments.

items.title: DiscernBench: Evaluating Cooperative Discernment of LLM Agents in Institutional Settings
items.summary: Researchers introduce DiscernBench, evaluating eight LLMs on whether agents comply with, refuse, or escalate requests in institutional scenarios drawn from real incident reports.
items.why: Agents operating under institutional constraints need judgment about refusal and escalation, which this benchmark tests across eight models.

items.title: When do stored facts become available in looped transformers?
items.summary: Researchers study how depth-resolved factual information becomes readable in looped transformers across synthetic factual recall and multi-hop reasoning tasks.
items.why: Understanding when stored facts surface in looped architectures informs design choices for recurrent-depth models.

items.title: Improving semantic equivalence in research-level math formalization
items.summary: Researchers collected 4,076 audited examples of changes between natural-language math and Lean formalizations to study semantic equivalence in autoformalization.
items.why: Training on documented formalization changes could improve tools that translate research mathematics into verified Lean code.

items.title: Does a Frontier Large Language Model Know What It Can Solve? A 100-Conjecture Calibration Study
items.summary: A study reports ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Ultra's confidence calibration on 100 open conjectures in geometric analysis, after 13 questions were excluded following an audit.
items.why: Calibration results on open research problems show how far model self-assessed success probabilities can be trusted.

items.title: EA-Bench: Measuring information and action efficiency under imperfect instructions
items.summary: Researchers introduced EA-Bench, a benchmark measuring how efficiently personal agents make tool calls and user interactions when instructions are incomplete or distracting.
items.why: It targets a real gap: agents waste tool calls and user turns on imperfect instructions, which matters for cost and UX in deployed agents.

items.title: Guarding with Judgment: Learning to Intervene for Multimodal Safety
items.summary: Researchers propose a multimodal safety approach letting models allow, warn, review, or refuse, plus a 20,126-audit corpus and the JudiBench benchmark.
items.why: Replacing binary refusals with graded actions could reduce unnecessary blocking while still handling visually unsafe requests.

items.title: FormaFin: Verifiable Financial Analysis with Solver-Guided Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: FormaFin trains small open language models to translate financial rules into SMT formulas, enabling formal verification of LLM-generated financial analyses.
items.why: Small local models that verify financial reasoning could suit confidential data where cloud models are not an option.

items.title: StudioBench: Benchmarking Agentic Multimodal Large Language Models for Productive Audiovisual Creation
items.summary: StudioBench is a 160-task benchmark testing general multimodal LLMs on end-to-end audiovisual creation spanning visuals, sound, and editing.
items.why: It measures whether general models can produce finished multi-stage video works, a capability gap relevant to creative tooling decisions.

items.title: STRIDE: Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-Guided Skill Disclosure and Evolution for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: STRIDE proposes separating stable strategies from tactical skills in skill-augmented reinforcement learning for LLM agents, retrieving tactics only at execution gaps.
items.why: Structured skill retrieval may improve how RL-trained agents reuse experience across episodes.

items.title: When Do Better Visual World Models Make Better Plans? Decision-Aligned Selection for Latent Planning
items.summary: The paper finds that reducing decision-relevant residual error in visual world models improves action selection more than reducing raw prediction error, and proposes a decision-aligned selection method.
items.why: Training objectives that target ranking quality rather than prediction accuracy may yield better planning for robotics and agents.

items.title: OmniDecisionBench: Evaluating and Benchmarking the Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models
items.summary: OmniDecisionBench is a holistic benchmark comparing multimodal System One decision models with general VLMs across 45 datasets and five capability families.
items.why: It offers a structured comparison of decision-style multimodal models against general VLMs, useful when choosing models for visual classification tasks.

items.title: STEdgeFormer: MCU and NPU Deployable Transformer Architecture
items.summary: STEdgeFormer is a transformer variant replacing self-attention with polynomial mixing and causal memory blocks, designed to run on MCU and NPU edge accelerators.
items.why: It addresses running sequence models on constrained edge hardware where standard self-attention is too memory-intensive.

items.title: PruneNAS: Constraint Aware Neural Architecture Search based Pruning
items.summary: PruneNAS integrates structured pruning into neural architecture search, generating candidates by pruning pretrained networks instead of training each from scratch.
items.why: Reusing pretrained weights could cut the high compute cost of architecture search for teams deploying models.

items.title: When Wrong Answers Remain Unsettled: Failure Dynamics in Recurrent Reasoners
items.summary: A study of a trained Hierarchical Reasoning Model finds wrong answers mostly remain unsettled under extra computation, while solved answers persist.
items.why: Findings on recurrent reasoner failure dynamics inform how inference budgets and stopping criteria are set, though the scope is a single small model on Sudoku.

items.title: Learning from Another Angle: Rotation-Based Test-Time Training for Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: RoTTT proposes rotation-based test-time training for multimodal LLMs to adapt to distribution shifts with less overhead than multi-sample approaches.
items.why: Cheaper test-time adaptation could make MLLMs more robust to shifted inputs without heavy inference costs.

items.title: Do You Even Know What I Want? Improving LLMs Ability to Detect Hidden User Intent
items.summary: The paper examines why LLMs fail to detect hidden user intent and seeks ways to improve their willingness to ask clarifying questions about objectives.
items.why: Misspecified goals cause agent misalignment and side effects, so better clarification behavior matters for agent reliability.

items.title: The Retry Tax: Why Static Same-Task Retries Can Cost More per Completion
items.summary: The paper analyzes static same-task retry policies for agents, showing retries can increase cost per completion as unresolved tasks skew toward harder ones.
items.why: Naive retry logic can quietly raise per-task costs, so teams running agents should model retry economics before adding attempts.

items.title: MVAgent: Per-Video Agents under Global Coordination for Multi-Video Understanding
items.summary: MVAgent separates per-video observation decisions from cross-video reasoning using a training-free multi-video understanding agent framework.
items.why: Splitting controllers keeps context from growing with every video, a design pattern relevant to long multi-input agent systems.

items.title: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds
items.summary: GameAnything is an open-source agentic platform that turns multimodal inspirations into playable game extensions, integrating coding agents with an automated playtester.
items.why: It shows coding agents combined with automated playtesting for game development, though the text gives little on evaluation results.

items.title: NoeVera: Can Knowledge Guide Experiments and Experiments Refine Knowledge?
items.summary: NoeVera is an agentic system that turns papers, code, benchmarks, and experiment results into a knowledge base to guide LLM serving optimization experiments.
items.why: It targets the harder problem of choosing which LLM serving configurations and mechanisms to test, not just predicting their performance.

items.title: Neural Agent Compiler: Learning to Schedule Soft Dependencies
items.summary: Researchers introduce Neural Agent Compiler (NAC), a method for scheduling soft dependencies, which are non-required information that can improve already executable LLM agent operations.
items.why: Current agent orchestration only handles hard dependencies, so this could improve how engineers schedule multi-step agent tool calls.

items.title: MetaSkill: Reusable Problem-Solving Methods for Adaptive Skill Orchestration in LLM Agents
items.summary: MetaSkill is a two-layer framework that lets LLM agents reuse problem-solving methods across tasks, selecting from 26 curated methods and binding roles to task objects.
items.why: It addresses how agents organize and adapt reusable skills, which matters for building more reliable agent workflows.

items.title: DoppelVet: Comparative Safety Verification for Self-Evolving Agents
items.summary: DoppelVet is a verification framework that checks proposed updates to self-evolving agents before they enter persistent memory or skill state.
items.why: Two updates can look identical to a verifier yet have opposite safety outcomes, so update checks need more than the evidence alone.

items.title: EMIP: Embodied Multi-Party Interaction Platform
items.summary: EMIP is a Minecraft-based virtual platform connecting multiple humans and AI agents for full-duplex speech and simultaneous physical actions in a shared environment.
items.why: It offers a testbed for studying human-AI cooperation in embodied settings, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: SAE-Audit: Clinical-Trial Prediction via Inference-Time Optimization of Black-Box LLMs Audited by Sparse Autoencoder Evidence
items.summary: SAE-Audit optimizes black-box LLMs at inference time for clinical-trial outcome prediction, audited using sparse autoencoder evidence, after finding frontier LLMs only modestly above chance.
items.why: It highlights that LLM predictions in high-stakes domains can be unreliable and their rationales may not reflect underlying evidence.

items.title: Emotion-Aware and Context-Grounded Dialogue Agents for Personalized Video Game Interactions
items.summary: ChatNPC is a game companion that personalizes dialogue in real time based on players' emotional shifts, using LLM tool-calling to retrieve memory and in-game context.
items.why: It shows how LLM tool-calling and memory can make game NPC dialogue more context-aware, though the text gives few evaluation details.

items.title: Layer-Level Control of Language Model Execution in Agent Frameworks
items.summary: Researchers propose a harness design exposing intermediate model layer states and execution controls to agent runtimes, demonstrated with a prototype that learns state-conditioned execution policies.
items.why: It suggests agent runtimes could allocate computation within and across models using internal states, not just prompt-response interfaces.

items.title: Scalar Tuned Lens Summaries Offer Limited Incremental Value for Mid-Generation Abstention
items.summary: A study finds scalar Tuned Lens summaries add limited value for mid-generation abstention, while raw intermediate-state probes improve ranking on MATH-500 across eight models.
items.why: It suggests engineers aiming to stop unpromising generations early should rely on raw intermediate states rather than scalar summaries.

items.title: Rethinking Closed-Ended Medical VLM Evaluation: From Stable Wrongness to Counterfactual Answer Sensitivity
items.summary: The paper identifies 'stable wrongness' in medical vision-language models, where incorrect yes/no answers stay confident and repeatable even when visual evidence is removed or mismatched.
items.why: Closed-ended benchmarks may hide reliability failures, so clinical deployments need counterfactual testing beyond accuracy scores.

items.title: Similarity-Constrained Reweighting for Complex Query Answering on Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: SCORE is a method for complex query answering on knowledge graphs that applies similarity constraints to arbitrary query variables, not only target variables.
items.why: It offers a more general and interpretable way to incorporate similarity constraints into knowledge graph reasoning queries.

items.title: Wactorz: Self-Writing LLM Agents That Discover, Repair, and Migrate at the Edge
items.summary: Wactorz is an open-source runtime where LLM-generated agents run as long-lived supervised actors that compile from chat requests and restart individually after crashes with state intact.
items.why: It targets agents that must run for months on edge hardware near sensors, a need most agent frameworks do not address.

items.title: Fin-RSI: A Unified Library of Financial Skills, Checks, and Self-Improvement for LLM Agents
items.summary: Fin-RSI is an open Python library of financial skills, checks, and self-improvement tools for LLM agents, with shared interfaces across models and agent frameworks.
items.why: It offers a unified interface for financial tooling that engineers can plug into LLM agent workflows across frameworks.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning from LLM-Generated (Suboptimal) Demonstrations
items.summary: Researchers use an LLM to generate a suboptimal advice policy that produces demonstration data at effectively no human cost, then use it to warmstart a DQN reinforcement learning agent.
items.why: It suggests LLM-generated demonstrations could reduce the cost and sample inefficiency of training RL agents from scratch.

items.title: Who Sent It or How It Moved? Sender Shortcuts in Cryptocurrency Anti-Money-Laundering Benchmarks, Audited on Elliptic2 and Elliptic++
items.summary: A paper audits Bitcoin anti-money-laundering benchmarks Elliptic, Elliptic++, and Elliptic2, testing whether models learn laundering patterns or merely identify senders.
items.why: It suggests reported performance on popular AML graph benchmarks may reflect sender shortcuts rather than detection of laundering behavior.

items.title: Dimension Is Free, Horizon Is Not: When Evolution Strategies Rival Policy Gradients for LLM Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Researchers analyze when Evolution Strategies match policy gradient methods like GRPO for fine-tuning LLMs, framing both as estimators of the same gradient differing in exploration.
items.why: Clarifies sample-efficiency tradeoffs between ES and PG for LLM fine-tuning, informing choice of training method at scale.

items.title: Latent-Predisposition Personas for Heterogeneous and Reliable LLM Survey Simulation
items.summary: Researchers find LLM persona-based survey simulations produce overly correlated opinions and inflated party-identification effects compared with humans, and test remedies for these issues.
items.why: Teams using LLM personas for survey or opinion simulation should know their outputs can be over-constrained and unrealistically coherent.

items.title: Blind to What They Can Fix: A Detection Gap in Self-Improving Agents
items.summary: A study finds self-improving AI agents that write runtime checks for their programs produce checks that stay silent when the environment changes, despite high task scores.
items.why: Runtime validation written by self-improving agents may not catch failures, so engineers should not trust agent-generated checks without testing.

items.title: Memphis: A Case Study in Seeding an Agent Task from a Model's Real-World Attempt
items.summary: Researchers propose seeding agent benchmark tasks from a model's own real-world attempt, using a case study where GPT-6.1 Sol managed human workers building desk lamps.
items.why: Suggests a method for building benchmarks that better reflect real-world failure modes of agents rather than just scaling up data.

items.title: Who Makes the Decision? Auditing an Agentic LLM Pipeline for Illicit Cryptocurrency Transaction Monitoring
items.summary: Researchers audit an agentic LLM pipeline for illicit crypto transaction monitoring on the Elliptic++ dataset, using decision-source attribution to show which component drives decisions.
items.why: Shows that end-to-end accuracy alone hides which pipeline component decides, which matters for auditing compliance systems.

items.title: MobileGrail: Learning Compact Guardrails for On-Device deployable Mobile GUI Agent Safety
items.summary: MobileGrail is a compact on-device guardrail model that checks mobile GUI agent actions before execution, avoiding sending screens to remote cloud servers.
items.why: On-device safety guardrails can protect private data like payments and messages without exposing every screen to a remote server.

items.title: Semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 and Gemini 3 Flash on H5N1 One Health questions
items.summary: A study measures the semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 and Gemini 3 Flash answers to 15 H5N1 One Health questions.
items.why: Shows how consistent chatbot answers are on health topics, a prerequisite for judging accuracy in high-stakes use.

items.title: Deep Discriminative Feature Fusion of Convolutional and Attention-Based Recurrent Representations for Subject-Independent ECG Stress Recognition
items.summary: Researchers propose a deep model fusing convolutional and attention-based recurrent features for subject-independent stress recognition from ECG signals.

items.title: Weight Averaging at Small Budgets Confounds Formula-Labeled Pretraining in Microstructure-Property Regression: A Pre-Specified Study with Post Hoc Rechecks
items.summary: A pre-specified study finds weight averaging at small label budgets confounds formula-labeled pretraining for microstructure-property regression with ConvNeXt-Small.
items.why: Highlights that small-budget fine-tuning results can be confounded by seed and averaging effects, relevant to evaluating pretraining claims.

items.title: Particle Belief Representations for Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability
items.summary: Researchers compare particle-filter belief encodings, including statistical summaries and permutation-invariant set encoders, as inputs to reinforcement-learning policies under partial observability.
items.why: Offers guidance on how to feed multimodal belief representations into fixed-size RL policies.

items.title: Second-Order Dynamics in Noisy RNNs Produce Exploration and Temporal Compression in Replay
items.summary: Researchers model spontaneous replay in noisy recurrent neural networks as Langevin sampling, explaining exploration and temporal compression seen in biological replay.

items.title: From Patterns to Threats: A Deep Learning Model for Anomaly Detection in Cyber-Physical Systems
items.summary: A deep autoencoder with a 38-24-12-6-12-24-38 architecture is trained on normal data from the Edge-IIoTset dataset to detect anomalies in cyber-physical systems.
items.why: Provides an application of autoencoder anomaly detection for industrial IoT security, though the abstract offers limited detail on results.

items.title: Reward Blindness: A Theoretical Framework for Diagnosing Reinforcement Learning Reward Limitations in Text-to-SQL
items.summary: A paper proposes a theoretical framework, Reward Error Sensitivity, to show how reward design in RL-trained text-to-SQL systems lets specific semantic errors survive training.
items.why: Suggests execution accuracy alone hides semantic errors, so teams training text-to-SQL should examine reward design more closely.

items.title: SAEPO: Sparse-Autoencoder-Guided Credit Assignment for Policy Optimization
items.summary: SAEPO uses sparse autoencoder features to guide token-level credit assignment in RLVR for improving LLM reasoning from sparse outcome rewards.
items.why: Offers a way to get finer-grained credit signals than outcome-only verifiers during reinforcement learning for reasoning.

items.title: When Learned IDS Model Selection Collapses to a Static Choice: A Measurement Study at the Edge
items.summary: On a Raspberry Pi 4B, a measurement study finds learned runtime model selectors for an IDS, tabular Q-learning and DQN, can collapse to a static detector choice.
items.why: Shows learned adaptive model selection may offer no benefit over a matched static detector, so edge deployments need controlled comparisons.

items.title: CARE-3D: Reinforcement Learning for Evidence Grounded Agentic Reasoning in Situated 3D Scenes
items.summary: Researchers propose CARE-3D, a reinforcement learning method that trains agents to ground evidence for reasoning about situated 3D scenes.
items.why: It targets rewarding useful intermediate tool choices rather than only final outcomes, which may inform how engineers train tool-using embodied agents.

items.title: Aligning Judge Models to Be Logically Consistent Multi-Rule Interpreters
items.summary: Researchers show judge models reach different conclusions when given a full ruleset versus judging rules one at a time, and propose alignment to fix this.
items.why: Teams using LLM judges for compliance across many jurisdictional rules may get inconsistent verdicts depending on how rules are presented.

items.title: Differential Proteomics to XAI Rules: A SHAP-FOL-ILP Modeling for Lung Adenocarcinoma
items.summary: Researchers present an interpretable workflow combining proteomics, sparse logistic regression, SHAP attribution, and first-order logic rule learning for lung adenocarcinoma.

items.title: Categorical Foundations of AI Agents
items.summary: A paper gives a categorical foundation for AI agents, classifying transformers, agents, orchestrations, and choreographies with their coalgebras and algebras.
items.why: Offers a formal mathematical framing of agent composition, but the abstract gives little on practical implications for engineers.

items.title: OWE-Bench: A long-horizon benchmark for measuring real-world engineering
items.summary: Researchers released OWE-Bench, a benchmark of 26 long-horizon engineering tasks across software, physical engineering, ML, and scientific computing.
items.why: It scores models on speed, cost, and accuracy for realistic multi-hour engineering work, useful for evaluating agent capability beyond short tasks.

items.title: Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA) for Energy Market Settlements: A Machine and Reinforcement Learning-Based Approach
items.summary: Researchers propose ANNA, a machine and reinforcement learning framework that audits energy market settlements by prioritizing anomalies.
items.why: Shows automated anomaly prioritization applied to high-volume financial settlement auditing where rule-based manual review is slow and error-prone.

items.title: SWAM: State-aware World Action Model for Multi-Agent 3D Environments
items.summary: Researchers present SWAM, a state-aware world action model that tracks the evolving states of non-player characters in multi-agent 3D game environments.
items.why: Addresses keeping off-screen agent state consistent in interactive world models without relying on external maps or predefined transitions.

items.title: EVD-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for EEG-to-Image Decoding
items.summary: Researchers introduce EVD-Bench, a benchmark for EEG-to-image decoding that separates results by which participants' data systems were allowed to use.
items.why: Highlights that differing training-data scopes can make cross-system benchmark scores non-comparable, a point relevant to evaluation design.

items.title: Context-Grounded Skill Internalization for Vision-Language Agents
items.summary: Researchers study context misalignment in skill internalization for vision-language agents, where models learn to reference skills that were removed during fine-tuning.
items.why: Identifies a failure mode in a common fine-tuning pipeline for teaching agents skills without in-context guidance.

items.title: Correlated by Construction: Endpoint Choice and the Validation of Protein Screening
items.summary: Researchers describe an automated protein production and screening platform and test whether miniaturized metal-affinity assays transfer to rare-earth separation.

items.title: Post-Training Agents for Long-Document Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers post-trained the open-weight Kimi-K2.7 on 1,465 expert-authored tasks to improve reasoning over long professional documents.
items.why: Shows a concrete post-training recipe for long-context enterprise document tasks using rank-32 adapters on an open-weight model.

items.title: Small data machine learning: the trilemma of low-sample tabular regimes
items.summary: A paper examines the trade-offs in evaluating and tuning models on small tabular datasets, using SmallGBM and SmallMLP in simulations and six public datasets.
items.why: Shows cross-validation can overstate tuning gains on small datasets, which affects how practitioners should evaluate models.

items.title: Could This BE Any More Wrong? Teaching VLMs to Know What They Don't Know in Document Extraction
items.summary: Researchers derive per-field confidence scores for vision-language model document extraction from token log-probabilities on receipts and legal contracts.
items.why: Offers a low-cost way to flag likely extraction errors in structured document pipelines without extra model calls.

items.title: When Does Optical Context Compression Pay Off? A Decode-Aware Cost Analysis of Reasoning VLMs
items.summary: A study finds optical context compression makes reasoning VLMs decode 1.5-3.5x longer, which can make image input costlier than text for some models.
items.why: Engineers evaluating document compression for cost must count decode tokens, not just prefill tokens, when comparing image and text inputs.

items.title: iFeST: An Iterative Motion Correction Framework for Fetal Brain Diffusion MRI via Frequency-Spatial-Temporal Modeling
items.summary: Researchers present iFeST, an iterative motion correction framework for fetal brain diffusion MRI using frequency-spatial-temporal modeling.

items.title: WASP: Continual Weight Adaptation for Streaming LLM Personalization
items.summary: WASP is a recurrent framework that trains a shared hypernetwork to generate personalized LoRA adapters from raw user interactions, avoiding per-user optimization.
items.why: It offers a way to continually personalize LLMs with cheap adapter updates instead of costly per-user fine-tuning.

items.title: AutoSECO: Automated Skill Evolution for Cross-Problem Combinatorial Optimization with General-Purpose LLM Agents
items.summary: AutoSECO is an automated method that evolves reusable solver-development skills for general-purpose LLM agents writing combinatorial optimization solvers across problems.
items.why: It suggests agents can reuse learned development guidance across problems rather than relying on per-problem workflows.

items.title: ReVAgent: Multi-Agent Reasoning-Intensive Video Generation
items.summary: ReVAgent is a multi-agent framework that solves a problem, generates explanatory keyframes, and synthesizes instructional videos showing state changes.

items.title: Same Executions, Different Gaps: Judgment Rules in Web-Agent Evaluation
items.summary: A study finds that changing how web-agent judgments define success can remove most of a reported performance lead without changing rankings.
items.why: Engineers comparing web agents should check how success is judged, since evaluation rules can overstate confidence in reported gains.

items.title: Adopting AI Technologies without Traps: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework
items.summary: Researchers present a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework to study how to adopt AI technologies while avoiding traps such as job loss and skill decline.

items.title: VeriWorld: A Verifiable Visual SWE-Bench for Spatial Reasoning in 3D Environments
items.summary: VeriWorld is a benchmark for spatial reasoning in interactive 3D environments, with executable actions and deterministic verification for vision-language models.
items.why: It helps separate whether VLM failures come from perception or from reasoning, aiding diagnosis of spatial-task models.

items.title: CLIP-FMoE: Scalable CLIP via Fused Mixture-of-Experts with Enforced Specialization
items.summary: CLIP-FMoE integrates a mixture-of-experts architecture into CLIP fine-tuning, using isolated constrained contrastive learning to aim for specialization.
items.why: It targets lower sequential training overhead and preserved zero-shot performance when scaling CLIP-style models with MoE.

items.title: Learning Heterogeneous Reasoning in Large Language Models: From Mode Compatibility to Local Bottlenecks
items.summary: The paper studies whether standard supervised fine-tuning can learn heterogeneous reasoning mixtures from diverse teachers without explicit mode conditioning.
items.why: Teams pooling reasoning traces from multiple sources for fine-tuning may face learnability bottlenecks that this analysis addresses.

items.title: A statistical measure of trust in generative AI
items.summary: Researchers propose a trustworthiness framework that estimates per-token trust in generative AI by comparing model-internal confidence against an external expert reference.
items.why: Per-token trust estimates could help flag unsupported outputs where ground-truth labels are scarce.

items.title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation
items.summary: MMMem is a task-aware multimodal memory framework that lets agents consolidate experience from completed tasks rather than only storing and retrieving records.
items.why: Agents that learn from completed tasks could avoid repeating mistakes across long-term multimodal interactions.

items.title: MH-RAG-DIVE: Dynamic and Cost-Efficient Multi-Hop RAG Evaluation via Tree-Cached Dialogue Simulation
items.summary: MH-RAG-DIVE is a dynamic user-simulation framework for evaluating RAG systems in multi-hop, multi-turn conversations using tree-cached dialogue simulation.
items.why: It offers a more realistic and cost-efficient way to test RAG changes than single-turn evaluation.

items.title: PseuDRAGON: Knowledge-Guided Local LLMs for Financial-Data Pseudonymization in Closed Networks
items.summary: PseuDRAGON uses local LLMs with confirmed judgments, exact-name lookup, and learned rules to pseudonymize financial data in closed networks, tested on 92 columns.
items.why: It shows how reusing expert corrections can make local models more consistent for sensitive data workflows.

items.title: mini-psych-agent: Evaluating Human-Like Behavior in LLM Agents through Interactive Psychological Environments
items.summary: mini-psych-agent is a framework for evaluating human-like behavior in LLM agents using interactive psychological environments under varying compute and incentives.
items.why: Behavior depends on model, harness, and test-time compute together, so evaluations should vary these factors.

items.title: Trustworthy Speech-Based Autism Screening under Class Imbalance with Uncertainty-Aware HuBERT Ensembles
items.summary: Researchers propose an uncertainty-aware speech-based autism screening framework using HuBERT ensembles, LOSO cross-validation, balanced bagging, and MC Dropout.

items.title: Event-Driven Parameter Dynamics for Spatiotemporal Parameter-Update Application in Deep Learning
items.summary: Event-Driven Parameter Dynamics (EPD) separates update generation from application using accumulation, event-triggered release, and reset in neural network training.
items.why: It proposes an alternative to applying optimizer updates every iteration, which could matter for training efficiency research.

items.title: Cost-Sensitive Reversibility of Non-Deterministic Actions
items.summary: Researchers introduce cost-sensitive reversibility for non-deterministic actions, extending qualitative weak and strong-cyclic reversibility notions in FOND planning to also measure reversal cost.
items.why: Adds cost measures to action reversibility in planning under non-determinism, useful for engineers building planners that must weigh the price of undoing actions.

items.title: DMC-5: Dual-Model Collaboration with Cache-aware Context Compression for Long-horizon Agents
items.summary: DMC-5 proposes a dual-model collaboration approach with cache-aware context compression to manage ever-growing interaction trajectories for long-horizon agents.
items.why: Addresses rising context costs in long-running agents where specialized models lack cached-input discounts, a practical concern for agent cost and design.

items.title: TamperCert: A Benchmark for Detecting Text Tampering in Degree Certificates
items.summary: TamperCert introduces a benchmark for detecting text tampering in degree certificates, motivated by rising forgery cases in admissions, immigration and hiring.
items.why: Offers a benchmark for document forgery detection, relevant to teams building verification workflows for credentials, though the text gives little on results.

items.title: HWRE-Bench: Can LLM Agents Understand Hardware They Did Not Design?
items.summary: HWRE-Bench is a benchmark testing whether LLM agents can reverse-engineer implemented hardware artifacts such as layouts, netlists and protected simulation models.
items.why: Tests agent capability in the reverse direction of hardware design flows, relevant to EDA and hardware teams evaluating agents on unfamiliar artifacts.

items.title: Automated Call for Action: RAG-Based Environmental Law Enforcement Screening System
items.summary: Researchers present a RAG-based LLM system that helps environmental law inspectors screen emission events, using a steel producer's coke plants as a case study.
items.why: Shows a domain-specific RAG pipeline combining sensor data, weather and complaints for regulatory screening, a template for enterprise compliance tooling.

items.title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers
items.summary: A paper examines when and how LLMs can act as context engineers, generating instructions or experiences from offline trials to steer themselves without training.
items.why: Clarifies when LLM-driven prompt and context optimization works, informing engineers choosing automated prompt engineering approaches.

items.title: Reproducible by Seed? Not on GPUs: Batch-Dependent Non-Determinism in Text-to-Image Models
items.summary: Researchers show that fixing prompt and seed does not reproduce text-to-image outputs on GPUs, because results vary with batch composition and GPU type across six models.
items.why: Reproducibility of generative image pipelines breaks under batching and hardware changes, which matters for testing, evaluation and audit workflows.

items.title: Splitting Belief Bases Conditionally based on Constraints for c-Representations and their Solutions
items.summary: The paper introduces conditional constraint splittings to localize reasoning over conditional belief bases for c-representations, a form of Spohn ranking models.

items.title: Learning What to Change: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Educational Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose state-verified reinforcement learning for tutoring agents, targeting cases where agents give sound answers while silently corrupting course and learner state.
items.why: Highlights that text-level judging misses state errors in stateful agents, a reliability concern for engineers deploying tool-using agents that modify persistent data.

items.title: Interrogation Protocols for AI Control
items.summary: Researchers introduce interrogation protocols in which a weaker trusted monitor asks a untrusted AI agent questions about confusing actions to improve AI control.
items.why: Offers a monitoring technique for high-stakes agent oversight, relevant to teams designing safeguards for capable agents against a weaker trusted monitor.

items.title: JaxNaviSim: A GPU-Accelerated, Data-Driven Simulator and Learning Benchmark for Maritime Navigation
items.summary: JaxNaviSim is a GPU-accelerated, data-driven maritime navigation simulator and learning benchmark that simulates step-by-step vessel responses and collisions in ports.

items.title: Learning Multimodal Representations from Partially Paired, Small-Scale Data
items.summary: CAMEO is an adversarial learning framework that fuses modalities from small, partially paired datasets by combining pre-trained unimodal encoders with cross-modal latent alignment.
items.why: Enables multimodal fusion where paired data is scarce, relevant to biomedical and other teams with large unimodal datasets but few paired samples.

items.title: ActField: Learning Action Effects as Continuous-Time Latent Dynamics
items.summary: ActField is a continuous-time JEPA world model that learns action effects as an action-conditioned vector field integrated over physical time for embodied tasks.
items.why: Models action effects in continuous time rather than at discrete intervals, relevant to robotics and embodied AI researchers building world models.

items.title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce
items.summary: WeMM-Ecom is a family of multimodal LLMs from 0.8B to 35B parameters, a mixture-of-experts model with 3B active, tuned for WeChat e-commerce content understanding.
items.why: Shows a domain-tuned multimodal model family claiming general-purpose performance too, relevant to teams evaluating specialized e-commerce models.

items.title: Beyond the Black Box: A Diagnosis-Driven Agent for Interpretable MIP Solver Tuning
items.summary: APEC is a log-grounded agent that tunes mixed-integer programming solvers per instance, using profiler-like diagnosis to explain configuration choices rather than treating tuning as a black box.
items.why: Replaces opaque Bayesian tuning with explainable, per-instance diagnosis, useful for teams optimizing solver performance in operations research workloads.

items.title: Uncovering Hidden Behaviours in Language Models via Limited-Parameter Finetuning
items.summary: Researchers propose limited-parameter finetuning on target-behaviour examples to reveal hidden LLM behaviours that standard behavioural evaluations miss.
items.why: Offers auditors a way to surface hidden model behaviours that anticipated test scenarios would not catch, strengthening alignment audits.

items.title: How Many Parameters Does Forecasting Need? A Survey and Code-Level Audit of Lightweight Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: A survey and code-level audit examines lightweight long-term time series forecasting models against large Transformer and foundation models.
items.why: Suggests tiny forecasting models can stay competitive on standard benchmarks, relevant for teams forecasting on constrained hardware.

items.title: Skill-Composer: Requirement-Driven Skill Selection from Multiple Marketplaces
items.summary: Skill-Composer proposes selecting a set of agent skills from multiple marketplaces to cover a task's full requirement, rather than ranking individual skills.
items.why: Addresses redundant top-ranked skills in marketplaces, which matters for developers choosing which agent capabilities to install.

items.title: Testing Quantized KV-Cache Maintenance: Encoding Layout and Historical Restoration
items.summary: Researchers test whether fixed quantized KV-cache implementations preserve encoded state, measuring drift from repeated re-encoding in 4-bit HQQ on two small models.
items.why: Shows existing checks can miss layout-dependent drift in quantized KV caches, a concern for inference correctness engineers.

items.title: Can Cities Have Personalities? Introducing the SCD City Personality Assessment
items.summary: Researchers introduce SCD City Personality Assessment, which gives document-grounded ChatGPT city personas a Myers-Briggs-inspired 24-statement instrument.

items.title: Transport-Safe Evaluation of LLM Agents: Trajectory-Dependent Judge Error and Anytime-Valid Auditing
items.summary: Researchers show that LLM judge error rates measured once and reused can bias corrected success rates when judge errors depend on agent trajectories.
items.why: Warns that reusing a single LLM-judge error calibration across agents can produce biased rankings in agent evaluations.

items.title: Intent-Conditioned Argument Mediation for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Blocking Trusted-but-Unauthorized Arguments
items.summary: IntentFlow is a mediation layer that checks tool-call arguments against user intent and provenance policy, blocking trusted-but-unauthorized values.
items.why: Targets a gap where provenance checks accept trusted values the user never requested, relevant for securing tool-using agents.

items.title: SchemaCaps: When a Compatible Tool Update Silently Widens an AI Agent's Authority
items.summary: SchemaCaps shows that compatible JSON schema updates to MCP tools can silently widen an AI agent's authority, and none of eight surveyed clients re-approves them.
items.why: Highlights that agent tools can gain permissions through routine schema changes without user re-approval, a security risk for agent deployments.

items.title: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games
items.summary: GameDojo is a benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 games for evaluating real-time interactive agents, with 600 hours of gameplay trajectories.

items.title: Unpacking the Evaluators: How Configuration Shapes the Evaluation of Alignment in Explainable AI
items.summary: Researchers examine how design choices in alignment-based evaluation metrics for explainable AI bias the results when attribution maps are compared to ground truth.
items.why: Shows evaluation configuration can shift XAI alignment scores, so teams should report metric settings when comparing explanations.

items.title: AeroJEPA: A Two-Stage Framework for Aerosol Forecasting with Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning
items.summary: AeroJEPA is a two-stage joint-embedding predictive framework for regional surface PM2.5 aerosol forecasting that fuses sparse observations with meteorological data.

items.title: Aggregation Rules Induced by KL-Regularised Preference Dynamics on Networks
items.summary: Researchers study which aggregation rules emerge when agents align models to their own preference data via KL-regularised steps while observing one another on a network.

items.title: Self-Evolving Evaluation Environments for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: CUA-SEE is a closed-loop evaluation environment that co-evolves tasks and executable verifiers from rollout evidence to keep computer-use agent benchmarks discriminative.
items.why: Addresses saturating static benchmarks for computer-use agents, useful for teams measuring agent progress more reliably.

items.title: MedUIGym: Evaluating and Training GUI Agents for Clinical Workflows
items.summary: MedUIGym is an interactive environment with 15,739 tasks from 17 benchmark sources for training and evaluating vision-language agents on clinical EHR graphical interfaces.
items.why: Provides a large training and evaluation environment for GUI agents in clinical workflows, relevant to healthcare AI builders.

items.title: Triage Accuracy of Jev and Open-Weight System One Decision Models and Their Use for Early Emergency Recognition in Symptom-Assessment Applications
items.summary: A study evaluates 16 decision models on 233 synthetic and 10,000 real-world cases, finding the best triaged 72.1% of synthetic cases correctly.
items.why: Suggests probability-based decision models may be easier to evaluate than free-text LLMs for medical triage devices.

items.title: ComputeWise: Measuring and Fixing GPU Waste by AI Research Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce ComputeWise, an open benchmark measuring and reducing wasted GPU use by AI research agents, using a simulated GPU that replays recorded runs.
items.why: Agents' GPU spend dominates their token cost, so wasteful experiments carry large cost impact for teams running autonomous research.

items.title: AI-Assisted Auto-formalization for Trustworthy Scientific Computing: Case Studies and Lessons Learned
items.summary: Researchers report case studies and lessons from using AI coding and mathematics agents to auto-formalize problems for trustworthy scientific computing beyond pure mathematics.

items.title: Boltz-Flow: Generating High-Quality Robot Action from Boltzmann Machine
items.summary: Boltz-Flow proposes replacing the fixed Gaussian source in flow-matching robot policies with a learned, observation- and instruction-conditioned distribution to improve action generation.

items.title: Grower-in-the-loop AI for Deployable Precision Fertilisation in Sustainable Agriculture
items.summary: Researchers present a grower-in-the-loop AI system for precision nitrogen fertilisation that accounts for on-farm constraints such as weather delays, machinery availability and budgets.

items.title: Automatic Occupational Coding through Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: Researchers propose using retrieval-augmented generation to automatically assign occupational codes to free-text job descriptions for linking workers to hazardous exposures.

items.title: Decoupling Solving from Abstention: Single-Rollout Conformal Risk Control for Hard-Budget LLM Reasoning
items.summary: Tail-CRC is proposed as a single-rollout conformal risk control method that helps LLMs decide when to abstain under hard token budgets during reasoning.
items.why: Offers error-controlled abstention for budget-limited LLM reasoning without the inference cost of multi-sample conformal methods.

items.title: AlphaDefect: Expert-Level AI for Slay the Spire 2
items.summary: AlphaDefect is an AI system trained with PPO that plays the deck-building game Slay the Spire 2 at expert level, winning 62-77% of runs at the highest difficulty.

items.title: ChiProgramBench: Can LLM Agents Rebuild Efficient Circuits from Pin-Level Experiments?
items.summary: ChiProgramBench is a benchmark of 18 hardware tasks testing whether LLM agents can rebuild efficient circuits by experimenting only through the pins of a hidden simulated reference.
items.why: Shows how agents perform on black-box hardware reverse engineering, a gap relevant to teams evaluating agents for hardware design work.

items.title: Orthogonally Mixed Sign Coding with Progressive Residual Refinement for Transformer Weight Compression
items.summary: Researchers propose a training-free progressive residual-sign quantization method using randomized orthogonal mixing to compress Transformer weights with flexible storage-fidelity trade-offs.
items.why: Offers a training-free way to trade storage for weight fidelity, which could matter for deploying compressed LLMs.

items.title: Revisiting Learning to Delegate: LLM Discovered Heuristics for Large-Scale Vehicle Routing
items.summary: Researchers use an LLM to autonomously refine heuristics that select subproblems for large-scale capacitated vehicle routing, enabling solver-based optimization of big instances.

items.title: Tradeoffs between objective outcomes and human enjoyment of work in human-AI task allocation
items.summary: A study examines tradeoffs between objective performance and workers' enjoyment when managers allocate tasks between humans and AI, such as assigning monitoring of AI outputs.

items.title: SayWhen: Set-Valued Semantic Commitment for Low-Regret Early Speech
items.summary: SayWhen introduces a test-time controller for early speech that commits to a task-directed act and uses a persistent veto to block release when later transcripts invalidate it.

items.title: LiveLoRA: Exact KV Cache Migration Across LoRA Updates for LLM Agents
items.summary: LiveLoRA proposes exact final-block KV cache migration so LLM agent sessions can switch LoRA adapter versions without replaying full interaction histories.
items.why: Avoids costly full-history re-prefill when updating adapters across many active agent sessions, reducing serving overhead.

items.title: Preflight: Agentic Last-Mile Verification for AI Software Supply Chains
items.summary: Preflight is a program-scoped verifier that synthesizes harnesses and records behavioral fingerprints to check how Python dependencies behave for a specific application before execution.
items.why: Targets supply-chain risk by checking how a dependency behaves within a specific application, not just its provenance or package-level behavior.

items.title: Self-Upgrading Embodied Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce self-upgrading embodied agents that learn from their own experience by editing their own weights during deployment, rather than relying on costly prompts or memory.

items.title: Genome-to-Image Translation: Reconstructing Escherichia coli Morphology from Genomic Sequences
items.summary: Researchers frame predicting E. coli colony morphology from whole-genome sequence data as a conditional image-generation problem, aiming to infer resistance traits.
items.why: Shows genomic data could eventually predict resistance phenotypes faster than culture-based testing, relevant to clinical ML pipelines.

items.title: Habitats: A Framework for Open-Ended Evolution of Agent Objectives
items.summary: The Habitats framework proposes open-ended evolution of executable agent objectives, maintaining a population of reward-policy pairs evaluated under every population reward.
items.why: Offers an alternative to fixed, predefined reward design by co-evolving what agents optimize with how they behave.

items.title: When Does Overriding the Majority Vote Help?
items.summary: A study of 150 competition-math questions tests when overriding a 16-response majority vote with extra reasoning, executed programs, or cross-model answers helps or hurts.
items.why: Gives guidance on when to trust alternative verification methods over simple majority voting in reasoning systems.

items.title: Reducing Order Sensitivity in Decision Models
items.summary: Researchers find that ten decision models are sensitive to option ordering, and compare eight methods to reduce this order sensitivity.
items.why: Order sensitivity can silently degrade accuracy in multi-step AI decision components, so mitigation matters for reliability.

items.title: Needwise: Generation-Free Conversational Recommendation from Need-Level Typed Decisions
items.summary: Needwise proposes a conversational recommender that uses typed decisions with option probabilities instead of LLM-generated text, avoiding re-reading dialogue each turn.
items.why: Suggests a faster, more interpretable recommendation design that avoids costly LLM ranking on every turn.

items.title: Know When to Abstain: Conformal Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL
items.summary: The paper formulates confidence estimation for Text-to-SQL as probabilistic query validation, separating query generation from validation using conformal methods.
items.why: Helps teams detect executed-but-wrong SQL queries at deployment, where gold queries are unavailable.

items.title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ
items.summary: Testing four open-weight models on 15,200 math problems, the study finds models steer on injected uncertainty tokens but fail to monitor their own confidence in situ.
